        "file": "tests/member_b_remediation/test_l1_trader_numeric.py",
        "patch": "Index: tests/member_b_remediation/test_l1_trader_numeric.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/member_b_remediation/test_l1_trader_numeric.py\t\n+++ tests/member_b_remediation/test_l1_trader_numeric.py\t\n@@ -1,117 +1,135 @@\n \"\"\"L1 — Trader numerical grounding (bounded prompt correction).\n \n Approved by the live-found Trader arithmetic error (C3 `20261121T093733Z-8c832879`:\n stop 255.33 described as ~1.5xATR/6.6 points below a 258.47 close with ATR 4.39,\n while the real difference is 3.14 = ~0.715xATR). These tests capture the actual\n Trader prompt on both the structured and free-text paths. They assert the\n instruction reaches the model; they cannot prove live model compliance.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n from unittest.mock import MagicMock\n \n import pytest\n from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n \n from tradingagents.agents.schemas import TraderAction, TraderProposal\n from tradingagents.agents.trader.trader import create_trader\n \n pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit\n \n MARKET_REPORT = (\n     \"AAPL closed at 258.47. ATR(14) = 4.39. Support 255.33, resistance 262.10. \"\n     \"The research plan claims the stop is roughly 1.5xATR (6.6 points) below the close.\"\n )\n INVESTMENT_PLAN = (\n     \"**Recommendation**: Underweight\\n\"\n     \"**Rationale**: momentum faded; the stop at 255.33 sits about 1.5xATR below 258.47.\\n\"\n     \"**Strategic Actions**: size against a standard allocation.\"\n )\n PORTFOLIO_BLOCK = (\n     \"Portfolio at the analysis date:\\n\"\n     \"These holdings and cash are user-supplied and unverified; treat them as the caller's \"\n     \"stated snapshot, not an authenticated account.\\n\"\n     \"- Current position in AAPL: 40 units, average price 190.00\\n\"\n     \"Available funds were not supplied; do not invent a balance or affordability.\"\n )\n \n \n def _state():\n     return {\n         \"company_of_interest\": \"AAPL\",\n         \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n         \"market_report\": MARKET_REPORT,\n         \"investment_plan\": INVESTMENT_PLAN,\n         \"portfolio_context\": PORTFOLIO_BLOCK,\n     }\n \n \n def _structured_llm(captured):\n     proposal = TraderProposal(action=TraderAction.SELL, reasoning=\"Fade.\")\n     structured = MagicMock()\n     structured.invoke.side_effect = lambda prompt: captured.__setitem__(\"prompt\", prompt) or proposal\n     llm = MagicMock()\n     llm.with_structured_output.return_value = structured\n     return llm\n \n \n def _fallback_llm(captured):\n     llm = MagicMock()\n     llm.with_structured_output.side_effect = NotImplementedError(\"no structured output\")\n     llm.invoke.side_effect = lambda prompt: (captured.__setitem__(\"prompt\", prompt)\n                                              or AIMessage(content=\"**Action**: Sell\\n\\nFade.\"))\n     return llm\n \n \n def _prompt_text(prompt) -> str:\n     return prompt if isinstance(prompt, str) else \"\\n\".join(m[\"content\"] for m in prompt)\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"builder\", [_structured_llm, _fallback_llm], ids=[\"structured\", \"fallback\"])\n def test_l1_01_numeric_grounding_reaches_model(builder):\n     captured = {}\n     create_trader(builder(captured))(_state())\n     text = _prompt_text(captured[\"prompt\"]).lower()\n \n     # General instruction to recompute distances/multiples from explicit anchors.\n     assert \"recompute\" in text or \"compute\" in text\n     assert \"atr\" in text\n     # Absolute distance and multiple guidance with the positive-ATR guard.\n     assert \"absolute\" in text or \"abs(\" in text\n     assert \"multiple\" in text and (\"positive\" in text or \"nonzero\" in text)\n     # Correct inconsistent upstream arithmetic rather than repeat it.\n     assert \"upstream\" in text or \"research\" in text\n     assert \"do not repeat\" in text or \"not repeat\" in text or \"correct\" in text\n     # Never assert guaranteed/locked gains.\n     assert \"guarantee\" in text or \"locked\" in text\n     # Omit unsupported ratios / say unknown.\n     assert \"unknown\" in text or \"omit\" in text\n     # Source values and portfolio facts are preserved.\n     for anchor in (\"258.47\", \"255.33\", \"4.39\"):\n         assert anchor in text\n     assert \"40\" in text\n     assert \"user-supplied and unverified\" in text\n \n \n def test_l1_01_no_hardcoded_observed_values_in_instruction():\n     \"\"\"The prompt must be general, not hardcode the observed 3.14/0.715 numbers.\"\"\"\n     captured = {}\n     create_trader(_structured_llm(captured))(_state())\n     system = \"\\n\".join(m[\"content\"] for m in captured[\"prompt\"] if m[\"role\"] == \"system\")\n     assert \"3.14\" not in system and \"0.715\" not in system\n     # Absolute-price/action/vocabulary constraints are unchanged.\n     assert \"absolute price\" in system.lower()\n     assert \"Buy / Hold / Sell\" in _prompt_text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n \n \n def test_l1_04_missing_atr_is_not_required_to_fabricate():\n     captured = {}\n     state = _state()\n     state[\"market_report\"] = \"AAPL closed at 258.47. Support 255.33; resistance 262.10.\"\n     create_trader(_structured_llm(captured))(state)\n     text = _prompt_text(captured[\"prompt\"]).lower()\n     # The instruction still asks to omit/mark-unknown unsupported ratios.\n     assert \"unknown\" in text or \"omit\" in text\n     # No ATR figure is invented into the prompt by our instruction.\n     assert \"atr(14) = 4.39\" not in text\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"builder\", [_structured_llm, _fallback_llm], ids=[\"structured\", \"fallback\"])\n+def test_l1_07_direction_instruction_reaches_model(builder):\n+    \"\"\"Compare level vs anchor before calling it above/below; avoid extra claims.\"\"\"\n+    captured = {}\n+    create_trader(builder(captured))(_state())\n+    text = _prompt_text(captured[\"prompt\"]).lower()\n+    # General direction rule: below when level < anchor, above when level > anchor.\n+    assert \"below\" in text and \"above\" in text\n+    assert \"anchor\" in text\n+    # Avoid unnecessary extra derived numeric claims not needed for the proposal.\n+    assert \"unnecessary\" in text or \"not needed\" in text or \"only the numbers\" in text\n+    # The anchors are still present and no observed numbers are hardcoded.\n+    for anchor in (\"258.47\", \"255.33\"):\n+        assert anchor in text\n+    assert \"0.72\" not in text and \"1.21\" not in text\n+\n",
        "additions": 18,
        "deletions": 0,
        "status": "modified"
      },

        "file": "tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py",
        "patch": "Index: tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py\t\n+++ tests/member_b_remediation/test_r2_scorer_correspondence.py\t\n@@ -1,529 +1,594 @@\n \"\"\"R2 — formal scorer must bind artifacts to the declared case, not just a Run ID.\n \n The review showed the scorer accepted inconsistent artifact/case/report evidence\n even with recomputed hashes. These tests build application-shaped synthetic\n evidence from the shared fixture helpers and mutate one fact at a time. Each\n defect must FAIL; the untouched complete population must still PASS.\n \"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import hashlib\n import importlib\n import importlib.util\n import json\n import sys\n from pathlib import Path\n \n import pytest\n \n pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit\n \n LIVE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / \"member_c_verification\" / \"live\"\n \n \n def _load_helper():\n     spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(\n         \"r2_exit_fixture\", LIVE_DIR / \"test_score_gov004_exitcodes.py\")\n     helper = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)\n     sys.modules[spec.name] = helper\n     spec.loader.exec_module(helper)\n     return helper\n \n \n @pytest.fixture\n def population(tmp_path, monkeypatch):\n helper.CHALLENGE_MARKERS.get(case)\n         for label in (\"a\", \"b\"):\n             rows.append(helper._make_run(\n                 root, case, f\"{case}-{label}\", challenge_marker=marker,\n                 challenge_reached=True if marker else None,\n             ))\n     helper._write_evidence(root, \"1\", rows)\n     scores = root / \"gov004_scores.json\"\n     helper._scores_all_pass(scores, [row[\"run_id\"] for row in rows])\n     return helper, scorer, root, scores, rows\n \n \n def _rescore_manifest(row):\n     path = Path(row[\"manifest_path\"])\n     row[\"manifest_sha256\"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n \n \n def _rescore_report(row):\n     path = Path(row[\"report_path\"])\n     row[\"report_sha256\"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n \n \n def _rewrite_evidence(root, rows):\n     (root / \"gov004_T1.json\").write_text(json.dumps(\n         {\"gate\": \"GOV-004\", \"kind\": \"formal\", \"trial\": \"1\", \"cases\": rows}), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n \n \n def test_r2_01_complete_synthetic_population_passes(population):\n     _helper, scorer, _root, scores, _rows = population\n     assert scorer.main([\"score\", str(scores)]) == 0\n \n \n def test_r2_02_explicit_empty_declared_no_portfolio_fails(population):\n     helper, scorer, root, scores, rows = population\n     row = next(r for r in rows if r[\"case_id\"] == \"GOV004-C2-explicit-empty\")\n     # Mutate the manifest to claim NO_PORTFOLIO for a case declared explicit-empty.\n     path = Path(row[\"manifest_path\"])\n     data = json.loads(path.read_text())\n     data.update(input_mode=\"NO_PORTFOLIO\", fingerprint_sha256=None,\n                 portfolio_as_of=None, as_of_basis=None, basename=None)\n     path.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     _rescore_manifest(row)\n     _rewrite_evidence(root, rows)\n     assert scorer.main([\"score\", str(scores)]) == 1\n \n \n def test_r2_02_held_target_substituted_for_empty_case_fails(population):\n     helper, scorer, root, scores, rows = population\n     row = next(r for r in rows if r[\"case_id\"] == \"GOV004-C2-explicit-empty\")\n     held = helper._case_identity(\"GOV004-C3-holdings-unknown-cash\")\n     path = Path(row[\"manifest_path\"])\n     data = json.loads(path.read_text())\n     data.update(input_mode=\"PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED\", fingerprint_sha256=held[\"fingerprint_sha256\"],\n                 portfolio_as_of=held[\"portfolio_as_of\"], basename=\"<in-memory>\")\n     path.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n     _rescore_manifest(row)\n     _rewrite_evidence(root, rows)\n     assert scorer.main([\"score\", str(scores)]) == 1\n \n \n @pytest.mark.parametrize(\"field,value\", [\n     (\"fingerprint_sha256\", \"b\" * 64),\n     (\"basename\", \"other.json\"),\n     (\"portfolio_as_of\", \"2026-01-08\"),\n     (\"as_of_basis\", \"FABRICATED\"),\n     (\"input_mode\", \"NO_PORTFOLIO\"),\n ])\n def test_r2_03_independent_provenance_mutation_fails(population, field, value):\n     helper, scorer, root, scores, rows = population\n     row = next(r for r in rows if r[\"case_id\"] == \"GOV004-C3-holdings-unknown-cash\")\n     path = Path(row[\"manifest_path\"])\n     data = json.loads(path.read_text())\n # --- cross-process exclusivity (R3-02/R3-06) --------------------------------\n \n _WORKER = r\"\"\"\n import sys\n sys.path.insert(0, {live!r})\n import replay_store\n root, run_id = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]\n try:\n     replay_store.claim_start(root, case_id=\"GOV004-C1-no-portfolio\",\n                              run_id=run_id, trial=\"1\",\n                              started_at_utc=\"2026-11-21T00:00:00Z\")\n     print(\"CLAIMED\")\n except replay_store.ReplayError as exc:\n     print(\"REFUSED:\" + str(exc)[:40])\n \"\"\"\n \n \n def _spawn_workers(store, run_ids):\n     import subprocess\n \n     script = _WORKER.format(live=str(LIVE_DIR))\n     procs = [subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, \"-c\", script, str(store), run_id],\n                               stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True) for run_id in run_ids]\n     return [proc.communicate(timeout=60)[0].strip() for proc in procs]\n \n \n def test_r3_02_concurrent_same_id_claims_are_exclusive(tmp_path):\n     store = tmp_path / \"evidence\"\n     store.mkdir()\n     outcomes = _spawn_workers(store, [\"same-id\"] * 8)\n     assert outcomes.count(\"CLAIMED\") == 1, outcomes\n     assert all(o.startswith(\"REFUSED\") or o == \"CLAIMED\" for o in outcomes), outcomes\n     # Exactly one retained record -- no lost update, no double claim.\n     records = [s for s in replay_store.load_starts(store) if s[\"run_id\"] == \"same-id\"]\n     assert len(records) == 1\n \n \n def ```text
All checks clean. The `AI-log` file remains coordinator-owned and untouched by me. Both corrections are complete with tests-first.

## 1) L1 direction clarification (`tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py`)

Extended the same bounded numeric-grounding instruction (inside the existing protected system prompt) to: compare a level with the explicit anchor before calling it above/below (`level < anchor` ⇒ below; `level > anchor` ⇒ above), and keep derived numbers to those actually needed (avoid unnecessary extra calculations). The abs-distance, positive-ATR, omit-unknown, no-guaranteed/locked-gains guidance and all absolute-price/rating/action behavior are preserved; no hardcoded fixture prices, no report rewrite, no new validator/Q rule.

Tests (`test_l1_trader_numeric.py`): captured actual-path regression on both the structured and forced free-text-fallback paths asserting the above/below direction rule and the avoid-extra-calculations guidance reach the model (anchors `258.47`/`255.33` present, no `0.72`/`1.21` hardcoding), while the existing supported missing/nonpositive-input tests remain. The observed “1.21% above the close” live failure is retained in the report as the target of this clarification; no live L1 PASS is claimed.

## 2) Tier-provider correspondence (R2, not a policy change)

Added `_tier_providers_match_fixed`: every tier's effective provider `(tier_provider or llm_provider)` must equal the fixed provider. Enforced for the recorded evidence config, the manifest `effective_config`, a pending start's captured binding, and the live preflight (zero calls on mismatch). Missing/`None` tier fields mean “inherit base” (legacy fixtures/normal configs remain valid); an explicit conflicting tier provider fails even with recomputed hashes/full scores.

Tests: wrong deep or quick provider in record, manifest, and pending binding → FAIL; inherited and explicit-`deepseek` tiers → PASS; actual-preflight rule exercised via the same helper before dispatch. Provider/model IDs and thresholds unchanged.

## Verification (actual)
- Focused offline (`member_b` + `member_c` + `member_d`): **314 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Full offline suite (one run after code stable): **1,726 passed, 2 skipped, 1 deselected; 100 subtests**.
- `ruff` clean; `pip check` clean; `git diff --check` clean.
- Docs updated precisely (evidence guide tier-provider paragraph; report L1 direction + observed live follow-up + tier-correspondence section, counts). Coordinator report sections and `AI-log` files untouched.

## Honest limits
Prompt-capture tests cannot prove live compliance; the coordinator will repeat all six real L1 fixture cases and the full fixed replay and inspect context. Historical F8 remains unverified (as Brian requested) and C's independent acceptance remains pending. No live/model calls, secrets, commits/pushes or governance edits from this process.

`READY_FOR_FINAL_LIVE_REPLAY`

- `"placeholder"` survives `Redactor` when no fake credential exists (benign-text R1-03);
- live-marker without opt-in, and non-live tests, still get placeholders; configured values preserved;
- exact `== "1"`/`0`/empty/`true` semantics pinned (R3-07 live-configuration criterion).

The three defect assertions failed against the pre-fix fixture (opted-in live still injected `"placeholder"`) and pass after.

## Boundaries honored
No production prompts/code changed this turn, no live/model calls, no secrets/.env/auth reads, no commits/pushes, no subagents, no governance/canonical-requirement edits. Historical F8 remains unverified and C's independent acceptance remains pending.

        "patch": "Index: docs/verification/gov004-evidence-package.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/verification/gov004-evidence-package.md\t\n+++ docs/verification/gov004-evidence-package.md\t\n@@ -1,81 +1,83 @@\n # GOV004 portable evidence and frozen population\n \n The November 18 historical live PASS remains **PENDING independent audit**: the original reports, manifests and score file are not present in this checkout. Repairing the scorer or creating fresh diagnostics cannot recover or approve those historical judgments. Preserve the original review and do not fabricate missing scores, timestamps or approval.\n \n ## Freeze a formal cohort before outcomes\n \n A/C must approve the actual provider/model configuration, applicability and critical-item policy before formal use. The scorer retains the documented fixed `deepseek` configuration; the saved school `openai_compatible` configuration is diagnostic until that difference is explicitly approved. Critical R1/R2/R3/R5/R6/R7 failures conservatively prevent PASS, regardless of optional caller flags. A/C should ratify this explicit policy rather than infer safety from a missing flag.\n \n Create `tests/member_c_verification/live/evidence/cohort.json` with:\n \n - `schema_version`: integer **2**. Schema 2 newly makes `ticker`/`analysis_date` mandatory; schema 1 is treated as stale and rejected (it is not silently upgraded).\n - `approved_by`: attributable real approver, never a generated identity.\n - `frozen_at_utc`: actual timezone-aware freeze timestamp, before the recorded run start.\n - `source_revision`: exact revision label, including `+dirty` where applicable.\n - `prompt_hash`: the application's full SHA256 prompt-source hash.\n - `ticker` and `analysis_date`: the **analysis controls** every formal attempt used. The live runner validates these (and the fixed configuration) against the selected run **before any graph call**, spending zero calls on a mismatch, and the scorer binds expected identity to them. A supported declared date (e.g. `2025-12-19`) is usable and is never inferred from a (possibly corrupt) manifest.\n - `members`: exactly ten objects with `case_id`, `trial` (`1` or `2`) and unique preallocated safe `run_id`. Each fixed case has one slot per trial.\n \n A full cohort that is malformed, stale or unsupported is rejected before dispatch. Expected per-case portfolio facts and `portfolio_kind` are derived from the authoritative `cases.py`, not duplicated in the scorer, so the definitions cannot drift.\n \n Retain the approval and cohort externally or in version control before execution; editable local timestamps alone cannot prove historical chronology. The application and capture harness record hashes, but that is not a digital signature or a substitute for review.\n \n Set `GOV004_TRIAL=1` or `2` for approved formal replay. The harness reads the cohort, uses its run IDs and refuses to reuse a started slot. A diagnostic run leaves the trial unset. Store diagnostic evidence separately from formal evidence. Every recorded formal start remains in overall completion accounting; retries do not replace failed cohort slots. Completion is reported separately from semantic scores on eligible completed reports.\n \n ### Isolated evidence root and live provider selection\n \n - **Isolation.** Both the scorer and the live replay honour `GOV004_EVIDENCE_DIR`. Point it at a fresh directory to replay without mixing old private pilot files; the replay writes `gov004_<stamp>.json`, its run tree, and the start ledger under that root, and `runner.outcome_to_dict(outcome, evidence_root=...)` records relative paths and hashes against it (an artifact outside the root is rejected). Example:\n \n   ```sh\n   GOV004_LIVE=1 GOV004_EVIDENCE_DIR=/tmp/gov004-live GOV004_TRIAL=1 \\\n     GOV004_TICKER=AAPL GOV004_DATE=2026-01-09 \\\n     .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/member_c_verification/live/test_gov004_live.py -p no:cacheprovider -q -s\n   ```\n \n - **Live provider override.** A narrowly-scoped `GOV004_LLM_PROVIDER` override is applied *after* the saved `.env` settings are restored. It changes the **provider only**: it sets the base provider and aligns both tier providers to it (so the effective adapter for every tier is the requested provider), and it does **not** rewrite the model IDs. Saved or caller-selected model IDs still reach the strict fixed-config validation, so a wrong model ID causes **zero** dispatch rather than being silently converted to a valid one. When unset, the saved settings are used unchanged. It never copies or migrates credentials (the caller supplies the provider's normal credential env var privately) and never lowers thresholds. Example: `GOV004_LLM_PROVIDER=deepseek` selects the `deepseek` provider/adapter for the base and both tiers; the model IDs from the saved/selected config (e.g. `CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`) are still validated against the fixed formal config.\n \n - **Truthful preflight.** Before any graph call the live runner validates the *entire* frozen cohort: schema 2 controls, safe run IDs, an ISO analysis date, a timezone-aware non-future `frozen_at_utc`, a revision/prompt-hash of the right shape, full slot coverage, the selected ticker/date and the fixed config. It also compares the declared `source_revision`/`prompt_hash` with the actual current source inventory (injectable for offline tests). A missing/malformed/stale/mismatching cohort spends **zero** calls and records no started run. Diagnostics never echo field values. The approval text is attributable caller authorization, separate from C's independent acceptance.\n \n - **Safe backend identifier.** The recorded `backend_host` is the URL's hostname only (via a real parser): `user:password@`, port, path and query are never persisted, and a malformed URL records `None`.\n \n - **Tier-provider correspondence.** The fixed formal provider must be the *effective* provider of **both** model tiers, not only the base `llm_provider`. The scorer requires `(deep_think_provider or llm_provider)` and `(quick_think_provider or llm_provider)` to equal the fixed provider in the recorded evidence config, the manifest `effective_config`, and a pending start's captured binding; the live preflight applies the same rule before dispatch. A missing/`None` tier field means \"inherit the base provider\" (legacy synthetic fixtures and normal configs stay valid); an explicit conflicting tier provider (e.g. `llm_provider=deepseek` but `quick_think_provider=openai`) fails even with recomputed hashes and full scores.\n \n - **Live credentials are not saturated by test dummies.** The shared pytest fixture `tests/conftest.py::_dummy_api_keys` normally substitutes `\"placeholder\"` for any missing provider key so offline tests never reach a provider. For an explicitly opted-in live run (`live` marker **and** `GOV004_LIVE=1`) it now skips that injection: the caller's real credentials are used unchanged, missing keys stay absent (so unconfigured auxiliary providers get no fake key), and the Redactor never inventories `\"placeholder\"` (which previously turned benign sentences like \"the feed returned a placeholder\" into \"[REDACTED]\"). All ordinary offline/integration/non-opted tests keep the placeholder behavior, and the upstream network block/blank-setting isolation are unchanged. This is a test-harness guard, not a production-code change.\n \n+- **Fundamentals period/source consistency (L2, prompt mitigation).** A live deepseek C1 report (`20261121T095453Z-2a60842e`) opened its Fundamentals section claiming a \"record fiscal Q1 (December 2025 quarter)\" yet later said no December-2025 income statement was present. The Fundamentals Analyst prompt now instructs: ground each period in the tool-reported period end (calendar date), fiscal label and filing date; never derive a calendar year by copying a fiscal-year label; apply the analysis-date cutoff (a filing dated after the analysis date is not yet known); do not claim a missing/unfiled period reported or invent an earnings-release date; and keep the opening summary, table and caveats consistent about which periods are available, stating stale/missing/unknown facts explicitly. No hardcoded figures/years, no data-source substitution, no new tools/checker/rating, output keys and delegation unchanged. This is a prompt mitigation verified by captured-path tests; live compliance is decided by contextual inspection (L2-02/03), not by the deterministic Q1–Q4 check.\n+\n Set `GOV004_TRIAL=1` or `2` for approved formal replay. The harness reads the cohort, uses its run IDs and refuses to reuse a started slot. A diagnostic run leaves the trial unset. Store diagnostic evidence separately from formal evidence.\n \n ## Record evidence and human scores\n \n The capture harness records portable relative report and manifest paths and their SHA256 digests. Manifests must match the run identity, result, source revision, fixed configuration, prompt hash and report path. Each report must contain the corresponding trusted Run ID header. A completed record needs all of this evidence; incomplete/error attempts remain counted even without completed artifacts.\n \n ### Case/provenance/report correspondence (R2)\n \n A complete set of score cells is not sufficient. The scorer now validates each completed attempt against the trusted frozen case definition, not against the attempt's own (possibly defective) record:\n \n - **Result conditions.** `COMPLETED` requires a valid rating, `stop_reason=null`, and `PASSED`/`NEEDS_REVIEW`; `REVIEW` requires `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `PASSED` carries no findings and `NEEDS_REVIEW` carries at least one valid Q1–Q4/`CHECK_ERROR` finding. A non-completed attempt carries no rating, a known stop reason, `NOT_RUN` and no findings.\n - **Case identity and analysis controls.** `ticker`, `analysis_date`, `input_mode`, `basename`, `fingerprint_sha256`, `portfolio_as_of` and `as_of_basis` must equal the values derived from the declared fixed case (from the authoritative `cases.py` via `expected_case_identity`, bound to the cohort controls). Expected input facts are never inferred from the manifest itself, so a held-target file substituted for the explicit-empty case, a `NO_PORTFOLIO` label on an explicit-empty case, or a wrong `portfolio_kind` fails even with recomputed hashes. Required manifest keys must be **present** even when their value is legitimately null (missing ≠ explicit null), and the manifest `schema_version` must be the supported application version.\n - **Authoritative report envelope.** The contiguous leading header block of `complete_report.md` (title, then the `- Key: value` lines, then `Findings:`) must agree with the manifest/record for run ID, ticker, analysis date, input mode, portfolio file, fingerprint, as-of/basis, run outcome, stop reason, final rating and output check. A missing, duplicate or conflicting authoritative field fails. Quoted (`>`), fenced (```) or later narrative that references a status is not treated as the authoritative block; a **bare, unquoted** authoritative-looking `- Key: value` line outside the header is rejected by a line/fence/quote-aware rule (not a global substring search).\n - **Durability mirror equality.** A per-attempt `gov004_attempt_<run_id>.json` mirror may repeat a run already counted from a batch file **only** when it is identical after parsing (full-row equality). A conflicting copy fails regardless of filename ordering; two genuinely independent attempts sharing a run ID still fail.\n \n Legacy formal evidence that lacks these fields is rejected rather than having the missing fields fabricated. This binds artifacts to the declared case; it does not cryptographically prove the honesty of a human score.\n \n ### Durable per-attempt accounting (R3)\n \n `tests/member_c_verification/live/replay_store.py` makes every attempt durable on its own. Before dispatch the whole selected cohort is preflighted (unique run IDs, one slot per case/trial, none already started); nothing runs on failure, and the live runner validates the frozen cohort controls/config first. Each slot is claimed (`STARTED`) in the versioned `gov004_starts.json` (schema 2) *before* `run_case` is called, carrying the pre-dispatch `model_config` and `controls` (ticker, analysis date, source revision, prompt hash), and its outcome is written to its own `gov004_attempt_<run_id>.json` (validated and confined to the evidence root), so two starts in one second cannot overwrite and a later failure cannot discard an earlier attempt. Only an **absent** ledger means “no evidence”: an empty/malformed/duplicate/unsafe ledger fails closed. `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`, and an application-reported `INTERRUPTED` result, stop further dispatch after the current start/outcome is preserved.\n \n A retained pending start is an **eligible**, noncompleted denominator entry only when its pre-dispatch binding is trusted and complete: a known fixed configuration and captured controls that match the frozen cohort (ticker, analysis date, and — where declared — source revision and prompt hash). A missing, unknown or mismatching binding is **ineligible yet still counted in the denominator**; it is never a completed quality sample, and model settings are never fabricated from a result. Acceptance requires **every** started attempt (completed or pending) to be eligible, so a wrongly-configured pending start blocks a PASS even when all completed rows are excellent (e.g. 10 completed + 1 defective pending → 10/11 ≥ 90% but FAIL). A genuine control-bound 9 completed + 1 pending (9/10 = 90%, ≥9 completed, ≥1 completed per case) passes at the unchanged thresholds. Reusing a started slot is refused. Diagnostics/pilot populations remain separate from the formal cohort.\n \n The score JSON contains a real `reviewer` and an `answers` list. Each applicable answer has `case_id`, `run_id`, `trial`, `item`, integer `score` (0 or 1), and a nonempty `citation` found in that run's report. Record rationale and disagreements alongside it. Do not submit N/A rows for inapplicable cells. The scorer derives applicability; missing, duplicate, unknown, incorrectly N/A or unrelated cells fail. Challenge markers and actual exposure must be retained and independently checked. Q1–Q4 NEEDS_REVIEW and human semantic judgments remain separate.\n \n ## Package and verify from a fresh checkout\n \n After sanitization and human review, run from the repository root:\n \n ```sh\n python tests/member_c_verification/live/package_gov004.py tests/member_c_verification/live/evidence /tmp/gov004-package --scores tests/member_c_verification/live/evidence/gov004_scores.json\n GOV004_EVIDENCE_DIR=/tmp/gov004-package python tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py /tmp/gov004-package/gov004_scores.json\n ```\n \n The destination must not already exist. The exporter copies only referenced reports/manifests and the cohort, evidence and scoring files, rewrites paths (including for the versioned `gov004_starts.json` start ledger and per-attempt `gov004_attempt_*.json` files), and emits `integrity.json`. Unresolved starts and all denominators survive the export. It refuses detected credential text rather than silently changing scored evidence. Review other sensitive content manually; automatic scanning cannot certify privacy. Move the package to a second path or fresh checkout (a different working directory) and repeat scoring; only relative artifact paths may be relied on. PASS=0, FAIL=1, PENDING=2. PENDING is never acceptance. Compare integrity hashes after transfer; retain the archive in an agreed durable location.\n \n The tracked ignore rules exclude private generated live evidence. Deliberate sanitized packages may be retained outside that tree after owner review. This workflow is not recovery of missing historical evidence and does not itself grant formal approval.\n",

These\n+tests capture the ACTUAL analyst prompt with synthetic dated evidence and assert\n+the general period/filing-cutoff/summary-consistency instruction reaches it.\n+Prompt capture only; live compliance is the coordinator's to inspect.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import pytest\n+from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, ToolMessage\n+\n+from tradingagents.agents.analysts.fundamentals_analyst import TOOLS, create_fundamentals_analyst\n+\n+pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit\n+\n+\n+def _capture_prompt():\n+    captured = {}\n+\n+    class _Bound:\n+        def invoke(self, prompt, *a, **k):\n+            captured[\"prompt\"] = prompt\n+            return AIMessage(content=\"report\", tool_calls=[])\n+\n+    class _LLM:\n+        def bind_tools(self, tools, *a, **k):\n+            captured[\"tools\"] = tools\n+            return _Bound()\n+\n+        def invoke(self, prompt, *a, **k):\n+            captured[\"prompt\"] = prompt\n+            return AIMessage(content=\"report\")\n+\n+    state = {\n+        \"company_of_interest\": \"AAPL\",\n+        \"trade_date\": \"2026-01-09\",\n+        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n+        \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n+        \"messages\": [\n+            HumanMessage(content=\"Analyze AAPL fundamentals.\"),\n+            ToolMessage(content=(\n+                \"income_statement: quarter ending 2025-06-28; \"\n+                \"balance_sheet: 2025-09-27; \"\n+                \"note: no income statement ending 2025-12-31 is available\"\n+            ), tool_call_id=\"call-1\", name=\"get_income_statement\"),\n+        ],\n+    }\n+    create_fundamentals_analyst(_LLM())(state)\n+    return captured\n+\n+\n+def _text(prompt):\n+    if isinstance(prompt, str):\n+        return prompt\n+    parts = []\n+    for message in prompt:\n+        content = getattr(message, \"content\", message)\n+        if isinstance(content, list):\n+            content = \" \".join(str(c) for c in content)\n+        parts.append(str(content))\n+    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n+\n+\n+@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"token\", [\n+    # explicit period-end / fiscal-label / filing-date grounding\n+    \"period end\", \"fiscal\", \"filing date\",\n+    # cutoff behaviour\n+    \"cutoff\", \"after the analysis\",\n+    # do not copy the fiscal-year label into the calendar year\n+    \"fiscal-year label\", \"calendar year\",\n+    # do not claim missing/unfiled periods reported; do not invent release dates\n+    \"missing\", \"do not claim\", \"earnings\", \"release date\",\n+    # opening summary / tables / caveats must agree\n+    \"summary\", \"caveat\", \"consistent\",\n+])\n+def test_l2_01_period_and_cutoff_instruction_reaches_prompt(token):\n+    captured = _capture_prompt()\n+    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"]).lower()\n+    assert token in text, token\n+\n+\n+def test_l2_01_tools_and_boundaries_preserved():\n+    captured = _capture_prompt()\n+    # Same tool tuple; instrument/date context still present.\n+    assert tuple(captured[\"tools\"]) == TOOLS\n+    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n+    assert \"2026-01-09\" in text\n+    assert \"AAPL\" in text or \"instrument\" in text.lower()\n+    # Delegation to decision agents is preserved.\n+    assert \"delegat\" in text.lower() or \"another agent decides\" in text.lower()\n+\n+\n+def _system_text(prompt):\n+    if isinstance(prompt, list):\n+        for message in prompt:\n+            if getattr(message, \"type\", \"\") == \"system\" or getattr(message, \"role\", \"\") == \"system\":\n+                return str(getattr(message, \"content\", message))\n+    return _text(prompt)\n+\n+\n+def test_l2_01_no_hardcoded_apple_figures_or_year():\n+    captured = _capture_prompt()\n+    system = _system_text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n+    # The instruction adds no specific fiscal figures/years; the only date is the\n+    # supplied analysis date.\n+    for forbidden in (\"2024-12-31\", \"2025-06-28\", \"2025-09-27\", \"December 2025\",\n+                      \"fiscal Q1\", \"FY2025\", \"FY2026\"):\n+        assert forbidden not in system, forbidden\n+\n+\n+def test_l2_03_source_values_are_not_rewritten_by_code():\n+    \"\"\"Supplied dated tool evidence is passed through unchanged, not normalized.\"\"\"\n+    captured = _capture_prompt()\n+    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n+    # The synthetic dated tool evidence survives to the model.\n+    assert \"2025-06-28\" in text and \"2025-09-27\" in text\n+    assert \"no income statement ending 2025-12-31\" in text\n+    # The prompt/instruction injects no fabricated latest-quarter figures.\n+    assert \"258.47\" not in text and \"255.33\" not in text\n",

  "content": "\"\"\"L2 — Fundamentals Analyst period/source consistency (bounded prompt repair).\n\nApproved by the live-found contradiction (deepseek C1 `20261121T095453Z-2a60842e`,\nas of 2026-01-09): the section opened claiming a \"record fiscal Q1 (December 2025\nquarter)\" yet later said no December-2025 income statement is present. These\ntests capture the ACTUAL analyst prompt with synthetic dated evidence and assert\nthe general period/filing-cutoff/summary-consistency instruction reaches it.\nPrompt capture only; live compliance is the coordinator's to inspect.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom unittest.mock import MagicMock\n\nimport pytest\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.analysts.fundamentals_analyst import TOOLS, create_fundamentals_analyst\n\npytestmark = pytest.mark.unit\n\n\ndef _capture_prompt():\n    captured = {}\n\n    class _Bound:\n        def invoke(self, prompt, *a, **k):\n            captured[\"prompt\"] = prompt\n            # A no-tool-call next turn would end the loop; return a tool call once\n            # then a final report, exercising the real take_turn path.\n            return AIMessage(content=\"report\", tool_calls=[])\n\n    class _LLM:\n        def bind_tools(self, tools, *a, **k):\n            captured[\"tools\"] = tools\n            return _Bound()\n\n        def invoke(self, prompt, *a, **k):\n            captured[\"prompt\"] = prompt\n            return AIMessage(content=\"report\")\n\n    state = {\n        \"company_of_interest\": \"AAPL\",\n        \"trade_date\": \"2026-01-09\",\n        \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n        \"instrument_context\": \"\",\n        \"messages\": [HumanMessage(content=\"Analyze AAPL fundamentals.\")],\n    }\n    create_fundamentals_analyst(_LLM())(state)\n    return captured\n\n\ndef _text(prompt):\n    if isinstance(prompt, str):\n        return prompt\n    parts = []\n    for message in prompt:\n        content = getattr(message, \"content\", message)\n        if isinstance(content, list):\n            content = \" \".join(str(c) for c in content)\n        parts.append(str(content))\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"token\", [\n    # explicit period-end / fiscal-label / filing-date grounding\n    \"period end\", \"fiscal\", \"filing date\",\n    # cutoff behaviour\n    \"cutoff\", \"after the analysis\",\n    # do not copy the fiscal-year label into the calendar year\n    \"fiscal-year label\", \"calendar year\",\n    # do not claim missing/unfiled periods reported; do not invent release dates\n    \"missing\", \"do not claim\", \"earnings\", \"release date\",\n    # opening summary / tables / caveats must agree\n    \"summary\", \"caveat\", \"consistent\",\n])\ndef test_l2_01_period_and_cutoff_instruction_reaches_prompt(token):\n    captured = _capture_prompt()\n    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"]).lower()\n    assert token in text, token\n\n\ndef test_l2_01_tools_and_boundaries_preserved():\n    captured = _capture_prompt()\n    # Same tool tuple; instrument/date context still present.\n    assert tuple(captured[\"tools\"]) == TOOLS\n    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n    assert \"2026-01-09\" in text\n    assert \"AAPL\" in text or \"instrument\" in text.lower()\n    # Delegation to decision agents is preserved.\n    assert \"delegat\" in text.lower() or \"another agent decides\" in text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_l2_01_no_hardcoded_apple_figures_or_year():\n    captured = _capture_prompt()\n    # The instruction adds no specific numbers/years; the only dates are the\n    # supplied analysis date.\n    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n    for forbidden in (\"2024-12-31\", \"2025-06-28\", \"2025-09-27\", \"December 2025\",\n                      \"fiscal Q1\", \"FY2025\", \"FY2026\"):\n        assert forbidden not in text, forbidden\n\n\ndef test_l2_03_source_values_are_not_rewritten_by_code():\n    \"\"\"Supplied dated tool evidence is passed through unchanged, not normalized.\"\"\"\n    captured = _capture_prompt()\n    text = _text(captured[\"prompt\"])\n    # The instruction must not inject fabricated figures for missing periods.\n    assert \"258.47\" not in text and \"255.33\" not in text\n",

        "patch": "Index: /home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md\n===================================================================\n--- /home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md\n+++ /home/brian/projects/CS5351/docs/reviews/remediation-r1-r5-2026-11-21.md\n@@ -73,20 +73,30 @@\n The real opt-in pytest replay exposed a test-fixture bug (not a production defect): `tests/conftest.py::_dummy_api_keys` injects `\"placeholder\"` for every missing provider key, and on a live run that fake value entered the application `Redactor` inventory, so benign sentences like \"the feed returned a placeholder\" became \"[REDACTED]\", and unconfigured auxiliary providers acquired fake keys. The direct production-boundary diagnostic did not show this because it does not run under the shared pytest fixture.\n \n Minimal repair (two-line guard in the parent fixture; explicitly in the allowed write set): `_dummy_api_keys` now skips dummy injection **only** when the test carries the `live` marker **and** `GOV004_LIVE` is exactly `\"1\"`. All ordinary offline/integration/non-opted tests keep the placeholder behavior; real (synthetic) provided keys are preserved; the upstream network block and blank-setting isolation are untouched; no `.env`/credential store is read. Tests (`tests/member_b_remediation/test_live_fixture_keys.py`) exercise the real fixture body with synthetic env: opted-in live leaves missing keys absent and provided keys unchanged; `\"placeholder\"` survives `Redactor` when no fake credential exists; offline/non-opted tests still get placeholders and preserve configured values; the exact `== \"1\"` enabled semantics are pinned. This complements the approved R1-03 benign-text and R3-07 live-configuration criteria. No production code changed.\n \n+## Live-found L2: Fundamentals period/source consistency (approved bounded repair)\n+\n+Live deepseek C1 `20261121T095453Z-2a60842e` (as of 2026-01-09) opened its Fundamentals section claiming a “record fiscal Q1 (December 2025 quarter)” yet later said no December-2025 income statement was present and warned not to assume the print exists. Downstream managers mostly recognised the gap, but the delivered contradictory analyst prose remains, and a PASSED Q1–Q4 result does not certify source/date consistency. Brian approved the bounded L2 plan ([`live-fundamentals-vintage-test-plan-2026-11-21.md`](../verification/proposals/live-fundamentals-vintage-test-plan-2026-11-21.md), actual response “Approve L2 tests and bounded repair”).\n+\n+**Change (implementer).** `tradingagents/agents/analysts/fundamentals_analyst.py` system prompt now instructs the analyst to ground each period in the tool-reported period end (calendar date), fiscal label and filing date; never derive a calendar year by copying a fiscal-year label; apply the analysis-date cutoff (a filing dated after the analysis date is not yet known); not claim a missing/unfiled period reported nor invent an earnings-release date; and keep the opening summary, table and caveats consistent about which periods are available, stating stale/missing/unknown facts explicitly. No hardcoded figures/years, no data-source substitution, no new tools/checker/rating; the tool tuple, instrument/date protection, output keys, language and delegation are unchanged.\n+\n+**Tests (implementer, offline).** `tests/member_b_remediation/test_l2_fundamentals_vintage.py` captures the actual analyst prompt with synthetic dated tool evidence: the period/fiscal-label/filing-date/cutoff/fiscal-year-copy/missing-period/earnings-date/summary-consistency instructions reach the model; the supplied dated evidence (`2025-06-28`, `2025-09-27`, the absent `2025-12-31` statement) passes through unchanged; the system instruction embeds no observed fiscal figures/years (`FY2025`/`FY2026`/`December 2025`, etc.). The 14 instruction-token assertions failed against the pre-change prompt and pass after.\n+\n+**Not claimed.** Prompt-capture tests cannot prove live compliance. The coordinator's three uniquely tagged real-model L2 generations (old December-2024/FY2025-Q1 report, latest income June-2025, September-2025 balance sheet, absent December-2025 income) plus missing/post-cutoff fixtures and the final ten-case replay are the coordinator's to run and inspect; no live L2 PASS is claimed here, and the instruction is mitigation, not a universal fact verifier.\n+\n ## Verification (actual final results)\n \n Environment: project `.venv`, Python 3.14, offline (`GOV004_LIVE=0`, `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`).\n \n | Check | Result |\n |---|---|\n-| `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short` | **1,733 passed, 2 skipped, 1 deselected; 100 subtests passed; 24 warnings.** Skips: opt-in live replay (unset) and optional Bedrock (`langchain_aws` absent). |\n+| `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short` | **1,750 passed, 2 skipped, 1 deselected; 100 subtests passed; 24 warnings.** Skips: opt-in live replay (unset) and optional Bedrock (`langchain_aws` absent). |\n | `.venv/bin/ruff check --no-cache . --output-format concise` | All checks passed. |\n | `.venv/bin/python -m pip check` | No broken requirements found. |\n | `git diff --check` | Passed. |\n \n-Focused offline set (`tests/member_b_remediation` + `tests/member_c_verification` + `tests/member_d_verification`) → 321 passed, 1 skipped before the full run (includes the 7 new live-fixture tests).\n+Focused offline set (`tests/member_b_remediation` + `tests/member_c_verification` + `tests/member_d_verification`) → passed with the new L2 tests before the full run.\n \n ## Honest remaining limits\n \n - **No Member C formal acceptance and no live semantic adjudication.** Offline prompt tests prove facts reach model input, not that live narratives comply; the C2 trim-language finding needs the approved provider.\n",

```text
The L2 bounded repair is complete and the only production change this turn is the Fundamentals Analyst prompt.

## L2 — Fundamentals period/source consistency (approved bounded repair)

**Production change** (`tradingagents/agents/analysts/fundamentals_analyst.py`, system prompt only): ground each period in the tool-reported period end (calendar date), fiscal label and filing date; never derive a calendar year by copying a fiscal-year label; apply the analysis-date cutoff (a filing after the analysis date is not yet known); do not claim a missing/unfiled period reported or invent an earnings-release date; and keep the opening summary, table and caveats consistent about which periods are available, stating stale/missing/unknown facts explicitly. No hardcoded figures/years, no data-source substitution, no new tools/checker/rating; tool tuple, instrument/date protection, output keys, language and delegation unchanged.

The observed live failure (deepseek C1 `20261121T095453Z-2a60842e`: “record fiscal Q1 (December 2025 quarter)” opening vs “no December-2025 income statement is present” later) is retained in the report, not erased.

**Tests** (`tests/member_b_remediation/test_l2_fundamentals_vintage.py`): capture the actual analyst prompt with synthetic dated tool evidence and assert every period/fiscal/cutoff/summary-consistency instruction reaches the model; the supplied dated evidence (`2025-06-28`, `2025-09-27`, absent `2025-12-31` statement) passes through unchanged; the system instruction embeds no observed fiscal years/figures (`FY2025`/`FY2026`/`December 2025`, etc.); tools and delegation preserved. The 14 instruction-token assertions failed against the pre-change prompt and pass after.

## Verification (actual)
- Focused offline (`member_b` + `member_c` + `member_d`): **338 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Full offline suite (one run after the code change): **1,750 passed, 2 skipped, 1 deselected; 100 subtests**.
- `ruff` clean; `pip check` clean; `git diff --check` clean.
- Docs updated: evidence guide (L2 period/source consistency note) and report (new implementer L2 subsection with the actual failure, change, tests, and pending status). Coordinator report sections and `AI-log` files untouched; no raw evidence edited.

## Boundaries honored / not claimed
Only the authorized analyst prompt production file changed; no other production changes, no live/model calls, no secrets/.env/auth reads, no commits/pushes, no subagents, no governance/canonical-requirement edits. R1–R5, L1 and the strict provider-tier/source controls remain intact. Prompt-capture tests cannot prove live compliance; the three uniquely tagged real L2 generations, missing/post-cutoff fixtures and the final ten-case replay are the coordinator's to run and inspect. No live L2 PASS is claimed; the instruction is mitigation, not a universal fact verifier. Historical F8 remains unverified and C's independent acceptance remains pending.

`READY_FOR_LIVE_L2_AND_FINAL_COHORT`
```

Completion is reported separately from semantic scores on eligible completed reports.\n \n ### Isolated evidence root and live provider selection\n \n - **Isolation.** Both the scorer and the live replay honour `GOV004_EVIDENCE_DIR`. Example:\n \n   ```sh\n   GOV004_LIVE=1 GOV004_EVIDENCE_DIR=/tmp/gov004-live GOV004_TRIAL=1 \\\n     GOV004_TICKER=AAPL GOV004_DATE=2026-01-09 \\\n     .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/member_c_verification/live/test_gov004_live.py -p no:cacheprovider -q -s\n   ```\n \n - **Live provider override.** A narrowly-scoped `GOV004_LLM_PROVIDER` override is applied *after* the saved `.env` settings are restored. Saved or caller-selected model IDs still reach the strict fixed-config validation, so a wrong model ID causes **zero** dispatch rather than being silently converted to a valid one. When unset, the saved settings are used unchanged. It never copies or migrates credentials (the caller supplies the provider's normal credential env var privately) and never lowers thresholds. Example: `GOV004_LLM_PROVIDER=deepseek` selects the `deepseek` provider/adapter for the base and both tiers; the model IDs from the saved/selected config (e.g. `CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`) are still validated against the fixed formal config.\n \n - **Truthful preflight.** Before any graph call the live runner validates the *entire* frozen cohort: schema 2 controls, safe run IDs, an ISO analysis date, a timezone-aware non-future `frozen_at_utc`, a revision/prompt-hash of the right shape, full slot coverage, the selected ticker/date and the fixed config. A missing/malformed/stale/mismatching cohort spends **zero** calls and records no started run. Diagnostics never echo field values. The scorer requires `(deep_think_provider or llm_provider)` and `(quick_think_provider or llm_provider)` to equal the fixed provider in the recorded evidence config, the manifest `effective_config`, and a pending start's captured binding; the live preflight applies the same rule before dispatch. A missing/`None` tier field means \"inherit the base provider\" (legacy synthetic fixtures and normal configs stay valid); an explicit conflicting tier provider (e.g. `llm_provider=deepseek` but `quick_think_provider=openai`) fails even with recomputed hashes and full scores.\n \n - **Live credentials are not saturated by test dummies.** The shared pytest fixture `tests/conftest.py::_dummy_api_keys` normally substitutes `\"placeholder\"` for any missing provider key so offline tests never reach a provider. No hardcoded figures/years, no data-source substitution, no new tools/checker/rating, output keys and delegation unchanged. This is a prompt mitigation verified by captured-path tests; live compliance is decided by contextual inspection (L2-02/03), not by the deterministic Q1–Q4 check.\n \n Set `GOV004_TRIAL=1` or `2` for approved formal replay. The harness reads the cohort, uses its run IDs and refuses to reuse a started slot. A diagnostic run leaves the trial unset. Store diagnostic evidence separately from formal evidence.\n \n ## Record evidence and human scores\n \n The capture harness records portable relative report and manifest paths and their SHA256 digests. Manifests must match the run identity, result, source revision, fixed configuration, prompt hash and report path. Each report must contain the corresponding trusted Run ID header. A completed record needs all of this evidence; incomplete/error attempts remain counted even without completed artifacts.\n \n ### Case/provenance/report correspondence (R2)\n \n A complete set of score cells is not sufficient. The scorer now validates each completed attempt against the trusted frozen case definition, not against the attempt's own (possibly defective) record:\n \n - **Result conditions.** `COMPLETED` requires a valid rating, `stop_reason=null`, and `PASSED`/`NEEDS_REVIEW`; `REVIEW` requires `NEEDS_REVIEW`; `PASSED` carries no findings and `NEEDS_REVIEW` carries at least one valid Q1–Q4/`CHECK_ERROR` finding. A non-completed attempt carries no rating, a known stop reason, `NOT_RUN` and no findings.\n - **Case identity and analysis controls.** `ticker`, `analysis_date`, `input_mode`, `basename`, `fingerprint_sha256`, `portfolio_as_of` and `as_of_basis` must equal the values derived from the declared fixed case (from the authoritative `cases.py` via `expected_case_identity`, bound to the cohort controls). Expected input facts are never inferred from the manifest itself, so a held-target file substituted for the explicit-empty case, a `NO_PORTFOLIO` label on an explicit-empty case, or a wrong `portfolio_kind` fails even with recomputed hashes. Required manifest keys must be **present** even when their value is legitimately null (missing ≠ explicit null), and the manifest `schema_version` must be the supported application version.\n - **Authoritative report envelope.** The contiguous leading header block of `complete_report.md` (title, then the `- Key: value` lines, then `Findings:`) must agree with the manifest/record for run ID, ticker, analysis date, input mode, portfolio file, fingerprint, as-of/basis, run outcome, stop reason, final rating and output check. A missing, duplicate or conflicting authoritative field fails. Quoted (`>`), fenced (```) or later narrative that references a status is not treated as the authoritative block; a **bare, unquoted** authoritative-looking `- Key: value` line outside the header is rejected by a line/fence/quote-aware rule (not a global substring search).\n - **Durability mirror equality.** A per-attempt `gov004_attempt_<run_id>.json` mirror may repeat a run already counted from a batch file **only** when it is identical after parsing (full-row equality). A conflicting copy fails regardless of filename ordering; two genuinely independent attempts sharing a run ID still fail.\n \n Legacy formal evidence that lacks these fields is rejected rather than having the missing fields fabricated. This binds artifacts to the declared case; it does not cryptographically prove the honesty of a human score.\n \n ### Durable per-attempt accounting (R3)\n \n `tests/member_c_verification/live/replay_store.py` makes every attempt durable on its own. Before dispatch the whole selected cohort is preflighted (unique run IDs, one slot per case/trial, none already started); nothing runs on failure, and the live runner validates the frozen cohort controls/config first. Each slot is claimed (`STARTED`) in the versioned `gov004_starts.json` (schema 2) *before* `run_case` is called, carrying the pre-dispatch `model_config` and `controls` (ticker, analysis date, source revision, prompt hash), and its outcome is written to its own `gov004_attempt_<run_id>.json` (validated and confined to the evidence root), so two starts in one second cannot overwrite and a later failure cannot discard an earlier attempt. Only an **absent** ledger means “no evidence”: an empty/malformed/duplicate/unsafe ledger fails closed. `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`, and an application-reported `INTERRUPTED` result, stop further dispatch after the current start/outcome is preserved.\n \n A retained pending start is an **eligible**, noncompleted denominator entry only when its pre-dispatch binding is trusted and complete: a known fixed configuration and captured controls that match the frozen cohort (ticker, analysis date, and — where declared — source revision and prompt hash). A missing, unknown or mismatching binding is **ineligible yet still counted in the denominator**; it is never a completed quality sample, and model settings are never fabricated from a result. Acceptance requires **every** started attempt (completed or pending) to be eligible, so a wrongly-configured pending start blocks a PASS even when all completed rows are excellent (e.g. 10 completed + 1 defective pending → 10/11 ≥ 90% but FAIL). A genuine control-bound 9 completed + 1 pending (9/10 = 90%, ≥9 completed, ≥1 completed per case) passes at the unchanged thresholds. Reusing a started slot is refused. Diagnostics/pilot populations remain separate from the formal cohort.\n \n The score JSON contains a real `reviewer` and an `answers` list. Each applicable answer has `case_id`, `run_id`, `trial`, `item`, integer `score` (0 or 1), and a nonempty `citation` found in that run's report. Record rationale and disagreements alongside it. Do not submit N/A rows for inapplicable cells. The scorer derives applicability; missing, duplicate, unknown, incorrectly N/A or unrelated cells fail. Challenge markers and actual exposure must be retained and independently checked. Q1–Q4 NEEDS_REVIEW and human semantic judgments remain separate.\n \n ## Package and verify from a fresh checkout\n \n After sanitization and human review, run from the repository root:\n \n ```sh\n python tests/member_c_verification/live/package_gov004.py tests/member_c_verification/live/evidence /tmp/gov004-package --scores tests/member_c_verification/live/evidence/gov004_scores.json\n GOV004_EVIDENCE_DIR=/tmp/gov004-package python tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py /tmp/gov004-package/gov004_scores.json\n ```\n \n The destination must not already exist. The exporter copies only referenced reports/manifests and the cohort, evidence and scoring files, rewrites paths (including for the versioned `gov004_starts.json` start ledger and per-attempt `gov004_attempt_*.json` files), and emits `integrity.json`. Unresolved starts and all denominators survive the export. It refuses detected credential text rather than silently changing scored evidence. Review other sensitive content manually; automatic scanning cannot certify privacy. Move the package to a second path or fresh checkout (a different working directory) and repeat scoring; only relative artifact paths may be relied on. PASS=0, FAIL=1, PENDING=2. PENDING is never acceptance. Compare integrity hashes after transfer; retain the archive in an agreed durable location.\n \n The tracked ignore rules exclude private generated live evidence. Deliberate sanitized packages may be retained outside that tree after owner review. This workflow is not recovery of missing historical evidence and does not itself grant formal approval.\n",

```text
The one small L2-03 clarification is complete, with the observed live failure retained and no L2-03 pass claimed.

## Change (same Fundamentals Analyst prompt only)

Added one general clarification to `tradingagents/agents/analysts/fundamentals_analyst.py`: excluded post-cutoff filing metadata, including its future filing date, cannot establish an earnings schedule or event timing; only independently supplied evidence available on or before the cutoff can support an upcoming report's date, and the excluded row/date may be quoted solely to explain exclusion, never to forecast timing — otherwise the date/timing is unknown. No hardcoded dates/figures, no new tool/classifier/schema/rating/provider-policy change; tools, report structure, source values, output keys and delegation preserved.

## Tests (first)

Extended `tests/member_b_remediation/test_l2_fundamentals_vintage.py` with a captured-path regression using synthetic future-filing metadata (excluded `2026-03-31` row filed `2026-01-29`, `$999` revenue): the schedule/event-timing/on-or-before-cutoff/quote-for-exclusion/unknown instruction reaches the model; the synthetic future date/`$999` row passes through to the model unchanged; the system instruction embeds no concrete future dates/figure. The six new instruction-token assertions failed against the pre-change prompt and now pass; the existing 21 L2 assertions remain green.

## Recorded findings (retained, not erased)

- Earlier L2: `20261121T095453Z-2a60842e` “record fiscal Q1 (December 2025 quarter)” opening vs “no December-2025 income statement” later.
- L2-03 live: post-cutoff case excluded the `2026-01-29` `$999` actuals but still used that future filing date to forecast an event “roughly three weeks after the analysis date”. Reported as an open L2-03 negative; **not** marked passed.

## Verification (actual)

- Full offline suite (one run after the code change): **1,760 passed, 2 skipped, 1 deselected; 100 subtests**.
- `ruff` clean; `pip check` clean; `git diff --check` clean.
- Docs-only updates since: evidence guide L2 note + report L2 subsection (change, tests, observed live follow-up, not-claimed). Coordinator report sections and `AI-log` files untouched; no raw evidence edited.

## Boundaries

Only the authorized analyst prompt changed; no other production code, no live/model calls, no secrets/.env/auth reads, no commits/pushes, no subagents, no governance/canonical-requirement edits. R1–R5, L1, and the strict provider-tier/source controls remain intact. No live L2 PASS claimed; the instruction is mitigation, not a universal fact verifier.

`READY_FOR_FINAL_L2_CHECK_AND_COHORT`

Actual live dispatch, narrative inspection, AI-assisted scoring proposals and evidence packaging are performed by the coordinator; they are not claimed here.\n \n ## Live-found L1: Trader numerical grounding (approved bounded repair)\n \n Coordinator live run `20261121T093733Z-8c832879` (C3) returned COMPLETED/PASSED but its delivered Trader section called stop `255.33` “roughly 1.5×ATR (6.6 points) below” a `258.47` close with ATR `4.39`; the real difference is `3.14` ≈ `0.715×ATR`. PM corrected it downstream, but the delivered Trader text stayed false. This actual failure is retained, not erased, and was not covered by the earlier offline prompt tests. Brian approved the bounded L1 plan ([`live-trader-numeric-test-plan-2026-11-21.md`](../verification/proposals/live-trader-numeric-test-plan-2026-11-21.md), actual response “Approve the test plan and bounded repair”).\n \n **Change (implementer).** `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py` system-prompt grounding now instructs the Trader to compute a stated distance/multiple from the explicit quoted anchors (`distance = abs(anchor − level)`, `multiple = distance / positive ATR`), to correct rather than repeat inconsistent upstream research arithmetic, to omit/“cannot be calculated” when ATR is missing or nonpositive, and not to call unrealised mark-to-market gains locked/guaranteed. It is general (no hardcoded observed prices), stays inside the existing protected system-prompt boundary, preserves all source/portfolio facts, and adds no tools, checker, Q5, enum, auto-rewrite or rating/action change. A small further clarification (feedback-7) tells the Trader to compare a level with the anchor before calling it above/below (level below the anchor is below it; level above is above it) and to keep derived numbers to those actually needed, avoiding unnecessary extra calculations.\n \n **Tests (implementer, offline).** `tests/member_b_remediation/test_l1_trader_numeric.py` captures the actual Trader prompt on the structured and forced free-text-fallback paths: the recompute/correction/positive-ATR/omit-unknown/no-guarantee instruction reaches the model alongside the `258.47`/`255.33`/`4.39` anchors and the 40-unit/user-supplied-unverified portfolio facts; the instruction hardcodes no `3.14`/`0.715`; a missing-ATR prompt does not invent an ATR figure while still instructing omit/unknown; and a captured regression asserts the new above/below direction instruction and the avoid-extra-calculations guidance reach the model on both paths.\n \n **Observed live follow-up (coordinator).** Real school-model L1 fixture calls were run immediately after the first prompt change. Three normal attempts and a forced free-text run correctly computed `258.47 − 255.33 = 3.14 ≈ 0.72×ATR` and rejected the prior `6.6`/`1.5` claim; missing/zero-ATR attempts did not invent a multiple. One missing-ATR output then said “Only 1.21% above the close” about a level that is actually below the close — a directional error in the same approved numerical-grounding scope, not a new checker feature. That actual failure is retained; the above/below clarification targets it.\n \n **Not claimed.** These are prompt-capture tests; they cannot prove live model compliance. The coordinator will repeat all six real L1 fixture cases and the full fixed replay and inspect context; no real L1 PASS is claimed here, and the instruction is mitigation, not universal mathematical verification.\n \n ## Tier-provider correspondence (feedback-7, R2)\n \n The fixed formal provider must be the effective provider of both model tiers, not only the base `llm_provider` (`(deep_think_provider or llm_provider)` and `(quick_think_provider or llm_provider)` select `deepseek`). Previously the scorer checked only `llm_provider`, so a record/manifest could claim `llm_provider=deepseek` while declaring a different tier adapter and still pass. The scorer now enforces the rule for the recorded evidence config, the manifest `effective_config`, and a pending start's captured binding, and the live preflight applies it before dispatch (zero calls on a mismatch). A missing/`None` tier field means \"inherit base\" so legacy synthetic fixtures and inherited configs remain valid; an explicit conflicting tier provider fails even with recomputed hashes/full scores. Tests cover wrong deep/quick providers in the record, manifest and pending binding → FAIL, and inherited/explicit-`deepseek` tiers → PASS. This is configuration correspondence, not a provider-policy change; provider/model IDs and thresholds are unchanged.\n \n ## Live-test fixture: credential/redaction contamination (feedback-8)\n \n The real opt-in pytest replay exposed a test-fixture bug (not a production defect): `tests/conftest.py::_dummy_api_keys` injects `\"placeholder\"` for every missing provider key, and on a live run that fake value entered the application `Redactor` inventory, so benign sentences like \"the feed returned a placeholder\" became \"[REDACTED]\", and unconfigured auxiliary providers acquired fake keys. The direct production-boundary diagnostic did not show this because it does not run under the shared pytest fixture.\n \n Minimal repair (two-line guard in the parent fixture; explicitly in the allowed write set): `_dummy_api_keys` now skips dummy injection **only** when the test carries the `live` marker **and** `GOV004_LIVE` is exactly `\"1\"`. All ordinary offline/integration/non-opted tests keep the placeholder behavior; real (synthetic) provided keys are preserved; the upstream network block and blank-setting isolation are untouched; no `.env`/credential store is read. Tests (`tests/member_b_remediation/test_live_fixture_keys.py`) exercise the real fixture body with synthetic env: opted-in live leaves missing keys absent and provided keys unchanged; `\"placeholder\"` survives `Redactor` when no fake credential exists; offline/non-opted tests still get placeholders and preserve configured values; the exact `== \"1\"` enabled semantics are pinned. This complements the approved R1-03 benign-text and R3-07 live-configuration criteria. No production code changed.\n \n ## Live-found L2: Fundamentals period/source consistency (approved bounded repair)\n \n Live deepseek C1 `20261121T095453Z-2a60842e` (as of 2026-01-09) opened its Fundamentals section claiming a “record fiscal Q1 (December 2025 quarter)” yet later said no December-2025 income statement was present and warned not to assume the print exists. A follow-up L2-03 observation added one small clarification: excluded post-cutoff filing metadata, including its future filing date, cannot establish an earnings schedule or event timing; only independently supplied evidence available on or before the cutoff can support an upcoming report's date, and the excluded row/date may be quoted solely to explain exclusion, never to forecast timing. No hardcoded figures/years, no data-source substitution, no new tools/checker/rating/classifier; the tool tuple, instrument/date protection, output keys, language and delegation are unchanged.\n \n-**Tests (implementer, offline).** `tests/member_b_remediation/test_l2_fundamentals_vintage.py` captures the actual analyst prompt with synthetic dated tool evidence: the period/fiscal-label/filing-date/cutoff/fiscal-year-copy/missing-period/earnings-date/summary-consistency instructions reach the model; the supplied dated evidence (`2025-06-28`, `2025-09-27`, the absent `2025-12-31` statement) passes through unchanged; the system instruction embeds no observed fiscal figures/years (`FY2025`/`FY2026`/`December 2025`, etc.). ```text
Now I'll rewrite the test file with a small set of meaningful scenarios. I'll capture the *system message specifically* (to avoid matching fixture payload) and separate a WRAP_UP helper.

Key design:
- `_capture(kind, ticker, date, tool_payloads, wrap_up=False)` returns `{tools?, system, all_text, invoke_called, ...}`.
- Scenario A (L2-01): regular tool path — tool tuple, dynamic ticker/date, full dated packet unchanged, and grouped system contract checks (all essential phrases checked together in the system message).
- Scenario B: WRAP_UP path — no `bind_tools`, `llm.invoke` called, dated ToolMessages preserved through `_as_text`, same system contract.
- Scenario C: missing-data + post-cutoff packets intact; code invents no figures/dates; exclusion/timing constraint specifically in system.
- Scenario D: different ticker/date → general, not Apple/year-hardcoded; system contains no fixture dates/figures.

Let me write it.

audit-only).\n+\n+No existing production module is modified in the audit-only first release (a later gated stage would touch `runapi/execution.py`/`reporting.py`/`checks.py` only with approval).\n+\n+### 4.1 `TrustedFact` / `FactBundle`\n+\n+```\n+FactSource = Literal[\"verified_market_snapshot\",\"portfolio_snapshot\",\"trader_structured\",\"fundamentals_statement\"]\n+\n+TrustedFact {\n+  name: str                      # e.g. \"close\", \"atr\", \"stop_loss\", \"fill\", \"target\", \"quantity\", \"cash\"\n+  value: Decimal | None          # None = unknown (never coerced to 0)\n+  unit: Literal[\"price\",\"points\",\"shares\",\"currency\",\"multiple\",\"percent\",\"ratio\"]\n+  source: FactSource\n+  as_of: str                     # ISO analysis date the fact is valid for\n+  period: str | None             # explicit period end/label if a statement fact\n+  precision: int                 # display decimals this fact was sourced at\n+}\n+\n+FactBundle {\n+  run_id: str; ticker: str; analysis_date: str\n+  fingerprint_sha256: str | None # frozen portfolio fingerprint when portfolio-derived (else None)\n+  source_revision: str; prompt_hash: str\n+  facts: list[TrustedFact]\n+  # coverage: which classes have complete inputs\n+}\n+```\n+\n+Rules: unknown `value` is `None` (never `0`); `as_of` must equal the run's analysis date (or earlier for statements); a fact with a post-cutoff `as_of`/`period` is excluded; the bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md)).\n+\n+### 4.2 `NumericClaim` (what the prose asserts)\n+\n+```\n+ClaimClass = Literal[\n+  \"price_distance\",\"price_direction\",\"atr_distance\",\"atr_band\",\n+  \"percent_with_denominator\",\"position_notional\",\"risk_reward\"\n+]\n+\n+NumericClaim {\n+  claim_id: str\n+  class: ClaimClass\n+  operands: list[str]            # fact names, resolved against the FactBundle\n+  asserted_value: Decimal | None # number the prose states (or None for a range/omitted)\n+  asserted_unit: \"price|points|currency|percent|ratio\"\n+  asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n+  anchor: str | None             # explicit anchor fact the distance/direction is relative to\n+  text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into the stage prose (evidence; not rewritten)\n+  stage: str                     # \"trader\" | \"portfolio_manager\" | \"research_manager\" | ...\n+}\n+```\n+\n+A claim with a unit/definition the calculator cannot bind is `UNSUPPORTED`, never silently reinterpreted.\n+\n+### 4.3 `ComputedResult` / `Finding` (proposal; NOT Q1–Q4)\n+\n+```\n+CoverageStatus = Literal[\"VERIFIED\",\"MISMATCH\",\"NOT_VERIFIABLE\",\"UNSUPPORTED\"]\n+\n+ComputedResult {\n+  claim_id: str\n+  computed_value: Decimal | None\n+  computed_unit: ...\n+  tolerance: Decimal             # absolute or relative per policy below\n+  status: CoverageStatus\n+  source_facts: list[str]\n+  notes: str                     # e.g. \"missing atr\" / \"unit multiplier vs points\"\n+}\n+```\n+\n+**Do not reuse `CHECK_ERROR`** to mean a numerical semantic mismatch and **do not create a Q5 silently.** A later, A/C-approved change may add a **proposal-only** finding type (e.g. `NumericFinding { rule: \"NUMERIC\", ... }`) with explicit compatibility notes; until then results live only in the sidecar artifact.\n+\n+### 4.4 Precision / tolerance / units policy (proposed, exact)\n+\n+- **Arithmetic:** `Decimal` with a fixed context precision (e.g. 28 significant digits); no binary float in the calculator.\n+- **Rounding for display:** half-up to the **sourced precision** of the weakest operand, or a class default (prices/points: 2 dp; multiples/ratios: 4 dp; percentages: 2 dp). Rounding is explicit and recorded.\n+- **Tolerance:** prices/points: `±0.01` (2 dp); multiples/ratios: `±0.005` relative after 4 dp; percentages: `±0.05` percentage points. A claim inside tolerance is `VERIFIED`; outside is `MISMATCH`.\n+- **Units:** the calculator refuses to combine a `multiple` operand with a `price/points` asserted unit — that is `MISMATCH` (dimensional/definition), reported to review, **not** a run failure and **not** auto-rewritten.\n+\n+### 4.5 Exact worked examples (deterministic; document examples)\n+\n+- Distance/direction: `close=258.47`, `stop=255.33` → `abs(258.47 − 255.33) = 3.14` points; `stop < close` ⇒ **below**. `VERIFIED` if prose says ≈`3.14` points below.\n+- ATR multiple: `distance=3.14`, `atr=4.39` (positive) → `3.14 / 4.39 ≈ 0.71526196`; display 4 dp `0.7153`, tolerance ±0.005 relative ⇒ prose “≈0.72×ATR” `VERIFIED`.\n+- ATR band: `1.5 × 4.39 = 6.585`, `2 × 4.39 = 8.78` points → band `6.585–8.78` points; display 2 dp `6.59–8.78` (half-up) or keep `6.585–8.78`. Prose “1.5–2×ATR is ~6.6–8.8 points” `VERIFIED` within ±0.01/±0.1 display tolerance as configured.\n+- **Observed failure:** prose “anchor the stop **1.5–8.8 points** below the fill” mixes a multiplier (`1.5×`) with a point quantity (`8.8 points`) → operands/units inconsistent ⇒ `MISMATCH` (dimensional), surfaced for review; the number is **not** silently rewritten and the run is **not** failed by the audit sidecar.\n+- Unsupported: effective tax rate from `net_income / operating_income` when `pretax_income`/`tax_expense` absent ⇒ `UNSUPPORTED` (definition) — never `VERIFIED`.\n+- Not verifiable: ATR missing or `≤ 0` ⇒ any ATR multiple/band claim ⇒ `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; unknown cash ⇒ any affordability claim ⇒ `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (no `0`).\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 5. Integration stages\n+\n+**Stage 0 — audit sidecar (no public change).** New `numeric/*` modules run after the engine returns `final_state` (and after a new trusted fact projection is built), producing `numeric_audit.json` under the run's staging dir alongside existing best-effort sinks. It writes **no** `Finding`, changes **no** `output_check`/`run_outcome`, and does not alter rendered text. Q1–Q4 unchanged. This is the first (and only immediately reviewable) release; ESTIMATE ~4–7 days.\n+\n+**Stage 1 — optional runtime gating / controlled rendering (needs approval).** Only if A/C approve a schema/interface/quality-rule change: surface coverage status in the report and/or map `MISMATCH` on a **registered** class to `NEEDS_REVIEW` via a **new, named** finding type (never a reused `CHECK_ERROR`, never a silent Q5). prose stop below (both direction cases) | direction correct both ways | claims |\n+| NVA-04 | prose “1.5–8.8 points below the fill” (observed) | `MISMATCH` (dimension: multiplier vs points), review-needed, not run-failure | calculator units |\n+| NVA-05 | ATR missing | ATR multiple/band `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; The goal is to choose up to **8 indicators** that provide complementary insights without redundancy. Categories and each category's indicators are:\n\nMoving Averages:\n- close_50_sma: 50 SMA: A medium-term trend indicator. Usage: Identify trend direction and serve as dynamic support/resistance. Tips: It lags price; combine with faster indicators for timely signals.\n- close_200_sma: 200 SMA: A long-term trend benchmark. Usage: Confirm overall market trend and identify golden/death cross setups. Tips: It reacts slowly; best for strategic trend confirmation rather than frequent trading entries.\n- close_10_ema: 10 EMA: A responsive short-term average. Tips: Prone to noise in choppy markets; use alongside longer averages for filtering false signals.\n\nMACD Related:\n- macd: MACD: Computes momentum via differences of EMAs. Usage: Look for crossovers and divergence as signals of trend changes. Tips: Confirm signals with other tools; prices may ride the band in strong trends.\n- boll_lb: Bollinger Lower Band: Typically 2 standard deviations below the middle line.
