        "text": "# Numeric-validation extension plan (PROPOSAL, unapproved)\n\nStatus: **PROPOSAL only.** Prepared 2026-11-21, Asia/Hong_Kong, by the OpenCode repair session at Brian's request (“Prepare a numeric-validation extension plan”, Codex call `call_2908c9d302df46eebfbf787d3853dcf3`). This authorizes **drafting a plan**, not implementing a validator, checker, schema, test, code change, canonical-requirement adoption or approval. Nothing here is an accepted requirement, a measured result, an independent score, or a Member C acceptance. Requirement IDs below use a separate **`NVR-`** prefix and are explicitly **UNAPPROVED**; they do not modify or renumber any `SEL-TA-*` ID.\n\nRelated existing documents (unchanged): [interface contracts](../interface-contracts.md), [invariants](../invariants.md), [runtime policy catalog](../runtime-policy-catalog.md), [ADR 001](../adr/001-portfolio-aware-cli.md), [memory design](../memory-design.md), [permission model](../permission-model.md), and the approved bounded prompt plans [`live-trader-numeric-test-plan-2026-11-21.md`](../../verification/proposals/live-trader-numeric-test-plan-2026-11-21.md) (L1) and [`live-fundamentals-vintage-test-plan-2026-11-21.md`](../../verification/proposals/live-fundamentals-vintage-test-plan-2026-11-21.md) (L2).\n\n---\n\n## 0. Deadline context and an optional small first slice\n\nThe course deadline is **26 Nov 2026, 23:59 Hong Kong**. The full programme in §7 is **not** proposed as an immediate, necessary fix and cannot be promised before the deadline. The frozen current-source live cohort and its source inventory must not be disturbed by this work; it is a separate, post-run audit proposal.\n\nAn **optional, small, bounded first slice** (see §6.0) is offered only if the team wants *something* reviewable quickly: a **standalone, post-run audit** run over already-saved artifacts, using an **explicitly supplied, run-bound typed input fixture**, covering only **price distance** and **price direction** and **ATR band**. It excludes LLM extraction, automatic typed extraction from the graph/snapshot, any staging integration, any report/UI change and any gating. It does **not** claim that any frozen report is already validated. Everything broader (§7 roadmap) is clearly **beyond** this immediately approved drafting work.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Problem statement\n\nPrompt instructions alone (L1/L2) reduce but cannot certify free-text financial arithmetic. The coordinator observed on the current frozen source (not re-run by this drafting session):\n\n- **L1 historical arithmetic (already mitigated by prompt, retained as history):** before the L1 prompt fix, the Trader described stop `255.33` as “roughly 1.5×ATR (6.6 points) below” a `258.47` close with ATR `4.39`; the real difference is `258.47 − 255.33 = 3.14` ≈ `0.7153×ATR`. L1 now yields the correct `3.14`/about `0.72×ATR` and “below” on the targeted fixtures.\n- **PM band wording (a unit/definition, not pure price arithmetic):** full C1 `20261121T101520Z-52544e6d` (deepseek profile) PM prose says a `1.5–2×ATR` stop is “~6.6–8.8 points (ATR 4.39)” and later writes **“anchor the stop 1.5–8.8 points below the fill.”** Both ends of the later phrase read as “points”; text alone cannot prove the leading `1.5` was meant as a multiplier. This is a **range mismatch against the explicitly anchored preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim** *only if* trusted context establishes that association; otherwise it is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **C2 ATR multiple (observed multiple error):** the final C2 PM described downside from `258.47` to `250.94` as “roughly 1×ATR” with ATR `4.39`. The actual move is `258.47 − 250.94 = 7.53`, and `7.53 / 4.39 ≈ 1.7153×ATR` — the “roughly 1×” wording does not match.\n\nThese are coordinator-observed examples used as **design coverage**, not an assertion that every claim in any report was independently audited, and not a re-run by this drafting session.\n\nBroader financial definitions also matter and are **not** trivially certifiable: EPS is not generally safely additive across quarters; an effective tax rate cannot be certified from net income / operating income when pretax income and tax expense are absent. A calculator can check a **relation relative to specified operands**; it cannot certify the truth, semantics or exhaustive extraction of financial prose.\n\n### 1.1 Proposed (UNAPPROVED) requirement IDs\n\nSeparate `NVR-` prefix; not canonical requirements.\n\n- **NVR-001 — Typed supplied facts first.** Numeric inputs are supplied to the auditor as a typed, run-bound fact bundle (ticker, analysis date, source identifier and availability date, period, units, declared precision) rather than parsed from prose. Automatic typed extraction from the graph/snapshot is a **later** change (§7), not part of the first slice.\n- **NVR-002 — Registered relations only.** A deterministic calculator evaluates only **registered** relations (see §4.2 roles) over `Decimal` (precision 28), with fixed units and defined rounding. No `eval`, no model-authored expected values. It verifies a relation against the **specified operands**; it does not certify the operands' truth or that the operand set is complete.\n- **NVR-003 — Bounded relation-class coverage.** The first slice covers only price distance, price direction and ATR band; the broader roadmap adds percentages with an explicit denominator, position notional from supplied quantities, and risk/reward with explicit anchors. Out-of-scope financial definitions (tax-rate from net/operating income, weighted-EPS derivation) are **`UNSUPPORTED`**, never “verified” merely because a formula runs.\n- **NVR-004 — Coverage-honest status.** Each **detected, registered** claim gets a status from `{VERIFIED, MISMATCH, NOT_VERIFIABLE, UNSUPPORTED}` (§4.3); there is **no** fifth per-claim `UNVERIFIED` status. Prose spans that are not detected/registered are counted separately, not scored. The denominator is only the **detected registered claims**, not every statement in the report. Partial coverage never yields a whole-narrative “verified” claim.\n- **NVR-005 — Standalone audit first.** The first slice runs **outside** the live run: a standalone post-run tool reads saved artifacts and a separately supplied typed fixture, and writes its own audit file (not into the finalized run directory). It changes **no** `output_check`, `run_outcome`, Q1–Q4, public enum, manifest or rendered report. Any staging integration, render/gating or public status change is separately unapproved.\n- **NVR-006 — Provenance and immutability.** Facts and claims bind to run id, ticker, analysis date, source identifier, source availability date, period, input fingerprint, unit and stage text hash+offset; unknown is never `0`; saved run artifacts are read-only. The audit's own retention/integrity is distinct from the authoritative report/manifest (which it never alters).\n\n### 1.2 Preserved decisions (not reopened)\n\nTwo input modes; five research ratings and three Trader actions; Q1–Q4 unchanged; user-supplied/unverified holdings/cash; no orders; source-date constraints; report+manifest critical, terminal-append best-effort; the frozen `RunContext`/fingerprint; no reliance on the raw low-level primitive. This plan does **not** restart the ADR 001 C1/C2/C3 architecture decision.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Candidate approaches (design comparison; ESTIMATE, no measurements)\n\nEstimates are design judgements labelled **ESTIMATE**. No measured latency/cost/accuracy is claimed.\n\n### 2.1 A — Expanded prompts only (status quo + more instructions)\n\n- **Rationale:** cheapest; no new modules. L1/L2 already show prompt wording changes behaviour.\n- **Coverage:** cannot certify arithmetic; unit/definition wording (e.g. the PM band, C2 multiple) can recur; no machine-readable coverage.\n- **Cost:** ESTIMATE ~0.2–0.5 day; low value as a correctness claim.\n- **Verdict:** necessary but insufficient; keep L1/L2, do not extend as the solution.\n\n### 2.2 B — Typed supplied-fact bundle + deterministic relation calculator + claim ledger (recommended)\n\n- **Rationale:** separates *facts* (typed, run-bound, supplied or later projected), *claims* (detected relations) and *computed results* (deterministic). A claim is checked **against the specified operands**; unregistered relations are `UNSUPPORTED`; missing/unknown/ambiguous inputs are `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **Coverage gaps:** undetected prose stays uncounted; semantic financial definitions remain `UNSUPPORTED`; coverage is bounded to the registered relations.\n- **Integration cost:** first slice (standalone, supplied fixture, three relations) small; automatic extraction, more classes and any staging/gating are later.\n- **Verdict:** recommended bounded design; do **not** restart C1/C2/C3.\n\n### 2.3 C — Prose parsing / second-LLM critique\n\n- **Rationale:** flexible; can “explain” arithmetic in arbitrary prose.\n- **Coverage:** a regex cannot universally verify financial prose; a second LLM is non-deterministic, adds cost/latency, can hallucinate agreement, and is itself unverifiable. It can at most **triage or extract candidate claims**, never certify.\n- **Cost:** ESTIMATE ~2–4 days plus per-call cost/latency; weak auditability.\n- **Verdict:** acceptable only as a *detection aid*; its output is always an `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`-until-confirmed suggestion and never yields `VERIFIED` by itself (wrong operands/formula that happen to compute must not certify the prose).\n\n**Recommendation:** **B**. Do not restart C1/C2/C3.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Actual code seams inspected (read-only)\n\n- **Graph state holds prose, not structured numbers.** `tradingagents/agents/state.py` (`AgentState`) carries prose reports and a rendered `portfolio_context` string; there is **no** typed numeric-facts field.\n- **The verified market snapshot is rendered text, computed transiently.** `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py::build_verified_market_snapshot` computes latest OHLCV + indicators deterministically but **returns a markdown string**; the structured values are not exposed to state. Tool: `tradingagents/agents/tools.py::get_verified_market_snapshot`.\n- **Some structured numeric fields exist for the Trader only.** `tradingagents/agents/schemas.py::TraderProposal` has `entry_price`, `stop_loss` and free-text `position_sizing`; the PM `PortfolioDecision.price_target` is similar. **These are the model's proposed levels, not verified external market truth.**\n- **Portfolio facts are caller input, not market data.** `tradingagents/portfolio.py::PortfolioContext` (user-supplied, **unverified**) and the frozen `RunContext`/`FrozenSnapshot` in `tradingagents/runapi/context.py` (fingerprint, as-of) are the only canonical account snapshot.\n- **Checks and result enums.** `tradingagents/runapi/checks.py::OutputChecker` implements Q1–Q4 only; `tradingagents/runapi/result.py` defines `Finding` rules `Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|CHECK_ERROR` and `OutputCheck = PASSED|NEEDS_REVIEW|NOT_RUN`.\n- **Envelope/report assembly.** `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py` builds the trusted envelope; `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py` builds the final markdown/HTML; `tradingagents/reporting.py::_report_parts` selects prose sections.\n\n**Consequence:** the code does **not** already expose a trusted structured numeric projection for price/ATR/position facts. A **new** projection (or, for the first slice, an explicitly supplied typed fixture) is **required**; this plan does not invent an existing canonical snapshot. A separate post-run audit can read the **saved** prose artifacts without touching the live path.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Proposed schema/interface (NEW; UNAPPROVED)\n\nFirst slice modules (out-of-tree standalone acceptable; paths proposed):\n\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/__init__.py` — package (NEW; D implements, B contract, C tests, E wiring).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/facts.py` — `TrustedFact`/`FactBundle` + precision/unit policy (NEW).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/calculator.py` — registered relations over `Decimal` (NEW).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/claims.py` — claim model + (fixture-supplied) claim set (NEW).\n- `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/audit.py` — standalone audit over saved artifacts + supplied fixture (NEW).\n\nNo existing production module is modified by the first slice.\n\n### 4.1 `TrustedFact` / `FactBundle`\n\n```\nFactSource = Literal[\n  \"supplied_run_fixture\",        # explicitly supplied, run-bound typed inputs (first slice)\n  \"verified_market_snapshot\",    # later: typed values derived from snapshot.py\n  \"fundamentals_statement\",      # later: statement facts with period/availability date\n  \"trader_proposed_level\",       # later: the Trader's *proposed* level (NOT verified market truth)\n  \"portfolio_user_supplied\",     # user-supplied holdings/cash (unverified)\n]\n\nTrustedFact {\n  name: str\n  value: Decimal | None          # None = unknown (never coerced to 0)\n  unit: Literal[\"price\",\"points\",\"shares\",\"currency\",\"multiple\",\"percent\",\"ratio\"]\n  source: FactSource\n  source_id: str                 # e.g. snapshot row id / statement ref / \"user_input\"\n  availability_date: str         # ISO date the fact became knowable (must be <= run analysis date)\n  period: str | None             # explicit statement period end/label (not the run date)\n  run_analysis_date: str         # the run's analysis date\n  declared_precision: int        # digits after decimal the claim may rely on\n  verified: bool                 # True only for externally-verifiable sources; user/model inputs are False\n}\n\nFactBundle {\n  run_id: str; ticker: str; analysis_date: str\n  fingerprint_sha256: str | None # frozen portfolio fingerprint when portfolio-derived (else None)\n  source_revision: str; prompt_hash: str\n  facts: list[TrustedFact]\n}\n```\n\nRules: unknown `value` is `None` (never `0`); `availability_date` must be `<=` the run analysis date (a post-cutoff fact is excluded); `period` and `availability_date` are distinct from the run date; `verified=False` for user-supplied holdings and for model-proposed levels. Portfolio **quantity is user-supplied/unverified**. The bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md)).\n\n### 4.2 `NumericClaim` (a detected relation) and calculator operations\n\n```\nClaimClass = Literal[\n  \"price_distance\",\"price_direction\",\"atr_distance\",\"atr_band\",\n  \"percent_with_denominator\",\"position_notional\",\"risk_reward\"\n]\n\nOperandRef {\n  fact: str                      # fact name in the bundle\n  role: Literal[\"anchor\",\"level\",\"atr\",\"minuend\",\"subtrahend\",\"numerator\",\n                \"denominator\",\"factor_min\",\"factor_max\",\"quantity\",\"price\"]\n}\n\nNumericClaim {\n  claim_id: str\n  class: ClaimClass\n  operands: list[OperandRef]     # roles make the relation explicit\n  asserted_unit: \"price|points|currency|percent|ratio|multiple\"\n  asserted_value: Decimal | None # single stated number, or...\n  asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n  asserted_direction: \"above|below|none\"   # for distance/direction claims\n  claim_precision: int           # digits after decimal the *claim* was stated at\n  anchor_evidence: str | None    # trusted reference linking a claim to its anchor claim, if any\n  stage: str                     # \"trader\" | \"portfolio_manager\" | \"research_manager\" | ...\n  stage_text_sha256: str         # hash of the stage prose the span indexes into\n  text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into that stage prose (evidence; never rewritten)\n  extraction_provenance: \"supplied\" | \"deterministic\" | \"llm_assisted\"\n}\n```\n\nA relation whose class is not registered, or whose operands cannot be bound, is `UNSUPPORTED` (the class exists as a typed marker even if the *specific* relation is unregistered; no impossible enum value). A claim with ambiguous extraction, unknown `claim_precision`, or missing `anchor_evidence` for an associated band is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n\n**Operations (fixed registry):** `subtract(minuend, subtrahend)`, `abs_distance(anchor, level)`, `direction(anchor, level)`, `divide_positive(numerator, denominator)` (denominator must be `> 0`), `scaled_band(factor_min, factor_max, atr)`. Each op declares its operand roles and result unit. The calculator **verifies the relation relative to the specified operands**; it does not assert that those operands are the true or complete facts.\n\n### 4.3 `ComputedResult` (proposal; NOT Q1–Q4)\n\n```\nCoverageStatus = Literal[\"VERIFIED\",\"MISMATCH\",\"NOT_VERIFIABLE\",\"UNSUPPORTED\"]\n\nComputedResult {\n  claim_id: str\n  computed_value: Decimal | None\n  computed_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n  computed_unit: ...\n  expected_at_claim_precision: Decimal | tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None  # round-half-up of computed at claim_precision\n  status: CoverageStatus\n  source_facts: list[str]\n  notes: str     # e.g. \"missing atr\" / \"ambiguous 1.5 role\" / \"unregistered relation\"\n}\n```\n\n**Do not reuse `CHECK_ERROR`** for a numerical semantic mismatch and **do not create a Q5 silently.** A later, A/C-approved change may add a proposal-only finding type (`NumericFinding { rule: \"NUMERIC\", ... }`); until then results live only in the standalone audit file.\n\n### 4.4 Precision / rounding / tolerance policy (exact for the first slice)\n\n- **Arithmetic:** Python `Decimal` at **context precision 28**; no binary float in the calculator.\n- **Comparison rule (first slice): NO tolerance.** Compute exactly, **round half-up to the claim's declared `claim_precision`**, and require **equality** with the asserted value/range endpoints. A different rounded value is `MISMATCH`.\n- **Precision bounds per class (frozen; a claim outside its bound is rejected as `NOT_VERIFIABLE`):**\n  - `price_distance`, `atr_band` → allow `claim_precision` in `{0,1,2}`.\n  - `atr_distance` (multiple) → allow `claim_precision` in `{1,2,3,4}`.\n  - `price_direction` → no numeric precision (boolean).\n- **Unknown/ambiguous precision** (the prose does not state enough digits to pin `claim_precision`) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **Units:** the calculator refuses to combine operands of incompatible unit roles (e.g. a `factor_*` (multiple) with a `points` asserted unit) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` unless trusted `anchor_evidence` explicitly links them as the same range claim, in which case they are compared as that claim (§4.5).\n- No caller-chosen wide tolerances are permitted in the first slice.\n\n### 4.5 Worked examples under this policy (document examples, exact)\n\n- **Distance/direction (positive):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=255.33`, ATR `4.39`. `abs(258.47 − 255.33) = 3.14`; direction: `255.33 < 258.47` ⇒ **below**. Prose “≈3.14 points below” at `claim_precision=2` → expected `3.14` → `VERIFIED`.\n- **Direction (negative):** same anchors, prose says “above” → computed **below** ⇒ `asserted_direction` mismatch ⇒ `MISMATCH`.\n- **ATR multiple (positive at 2 dp):** `3.14 / 4.39 = 0.7152619576…`; round half-up to `claim_precision=2` → `0.72`. Prose “0.72×ATR” → `VERIFIED`.\n- **ATR multiple (boundary negative):** same, but prose “0.7153×ATR” at `claim_precision=4` → expected `0.7153` (round-half-up of `0.71526195…`) → `VERIFIED`; prose “0.72×ATR” is only valid at `claim_precision=2`. A prose that states `0.72` but declares precision 4 is inconsistent → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (ambiguous precision), **not** silently accepted. This resolves the earlier `0.7153` vs `0.72` contradiction: the two are **different declared precisions**, compared by equality only at each claim's own precision.\n- **ATR band (positive):** `factor_min=1.5`, `factor_max=2`, `atr=4.39` → `1.5 × 4.39 = 6.585`, `2 × 4.39 = 8.78`. At `claim_precision=2`, round-half-up → expected band `(6.59, 8.78)`. Prose “6.59–8.78 points” → `VERIFIED`; prose “6.585–8.78” at precision 3 is outside the frozen bound for `atr_band` (max 2) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n- **ATR band (boundary negative):** prose “6.6–8.8 points” at `claim_precision=1`: expected (round-half-up) `(6.6, 8.8)` → `VERIFIED`; the **same** numbers claimed at precision 2 → expected `(6.59, 8.78)` ≠ `(6.60, 8.80)` → `MISMATCH`. Precision is part of the claim.\n- **PM band “1.5–8.8 points below the fill” (observed):** parsed literally, both endpoints are `points`, giving range `(1.5, 8.8)` points. If trusted `anchor_evidence` links it to the preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim, compare against the expected band `(6.59, 8.78)` at precision 2 → `MISMATCH` (lower endpoint `1.5` ≠ `6.59`). If no trusted association exists, the first endpoint's role is ambiguous (`1.5` could be a factor) ⇒ `NOT_VERIFIABLE`. It is **not** universally a dimensional error; the auditor reports `MISMATCH`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE` for review and never rewrites the text or fails the run.\n- **C2 ATR multiple (observed):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=250.94`, `atr=4.39` → `7.53`; `7.53 / 4.39 = 1.71526195…`; at `claim_precision=1` round-half-up → `1.7`. 17: ## 1. Problem statement
18: 
19: Prompt instructions alone (L1/L2) reduce but cannot certify free-text financial arithmetic. The coordinator observed on the current frozen source (not re-run by this drafting session):
20: 
21: - **L1 historical arithmetic (already mitigated by prompt, retained as history):** before the L1 prompt fix, the Trader described stop `255.33` as “roughly 1.5×ATR (6.6 points) below” a `258.47` close with ATR `4.39`; the real difference is `258.47 − 255.33 = 3.14` ≈ `0.7153×ATR`. L1 now yields the correct `3.14`/about `0.72×ATR` and “below” on the targeted fixtures.
22: - **PM band wording (a unit/definition, not pure price arithmetic):** full C1 `20261121T101520Z-52544e6d` (deepseek profile) PM prose says a `1.5–2×ATR` stop is “~6.6–8.8 points (ATR 4.39)” and later writes **“anchor the stop 1.5–8.8 points below the fill.”** Both ends of the later phrase read as “points”; text alone cannot prove the leading `1.5` was meant as a multiplier. This is a **range mismatch against the explicitly anchored preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim** *only if* trusted context establishes that association; otherwise it is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
23: - **C2 ATR multiple (observed multiple error):** the final C2 PM described downside from `258.47` to `250.94` as “roughly 1×ATR” with ATR `4.39`. The actual move is `258.47 − 250.94 = 7.53`, and `7.53 / 4.39 ≈ 1.7153×ATR` — the “roughly 1×” wording does not match.
24: 
25: These are coordinator-observed examples used as **design coverage**, not an assertion that every claim in any report was independently audited, and not a re-run by this drafting session.
26: 
27: Broader financial definitions also matter and are **not** trivially certifiable: EPS is not generally safely additive across quarters; an effective tax rate cannot be certified from net income / operating income when pretax income and tax expense are absent. A calculator can check a **relation relative to specified operands**; it cannot certify the truth, semantics or exhaustive extraction of financial prose.

29: ### 1.1 Proposed (UNAPPROVED) requirement IDs
30: 
31: Separate `NVR-` prefix; not canonical requirements.
32: 
33: - **NVR-001 — Typed supplied facts first.** Numeric inputs are supplied to the auditor as a typed, run-bound fact bundle (ticker, analysis date, source identifier and availability date, period, units, declared precision) rather than parsed from prose. Automatic typed extraction from the graph/snapshot is a **later** change (§7), not part of the first slice.
34: - **NVR-002 — Registered relations only.** A deterministic calculator evaluates only **registered** relations (see §4.2 roles) over `Decimal` (precision 28), with fixed units and defined rounding. No `eval`, no model-authored expected values. It verifies a relation against the **specified operands**; it does not certify the operands' truth or that the operand set is complete.
35: - **NVR-003 — Bounded relation-class coverage.** The first slice covers only price distance, price direction and ATR band; the broader roadmap adds percentages with an explicit denominator, position notional from supplied quantities, and risk/reward with explicit anchors. Out-of-scope financial definitions (tax-rate from net/operating income, weighted-EPS derivation) are **`UNSUPPORTED`**, never “verified” merely because a formula runs.
36: - **NVR-004 — Coverage-honest status.** Each **detected, registered** claim gets a status from `{VERIFIED, MISMATCH, NOT_VERIFIABLE, UNSUPPORTED}` (§4.3); there is **no** fifth per-claim `UNVERIFIED` status. Prose spans that are not detected/registered are counted separately, not scored. The denominator is only the **detected registered claims**, not every statement in the report. Partial coverage never yields a whole-narrative “verified” claim.
37: - **NVR-005 — Standalone audit first.** The first slice runs **outside** the live run: a standalone post-run tool reads saved artifacts and a separately supplied typed fixture, and writes its own audit file (not into the finalized run directory). It changes **no** `output_check`, `run_outcome`, Q1–Q4, public enum, manifest or rendered report. Any staging integration, render/gating or public status change is separately unapproved.
38: - **NVR-006 — Provenance and immutability.** Facts and claims bind to run id, ticker, analysis date, source identifier, source availability date, period, input fingerprint, unit and stage text hash+offset; unknown is never `0`; saved run artifacts are read-only. The audit's own retention/integrity is distinct from the authoritative report/manifest (which it never alters).

46: ## 2. Candidate approaches (design comparison; ESTIMATE, no measurements)
47: 
48: Estimates are design judgements labelled **ESTIMATE**. No measured latency/cost/accuracy is claimed.
49: 
50: ### 2.1 A — Expanded prompts only (status quo + more instructions)
51: 
52: - **Rationale:** cheapest; no new modules. L1/L2 already show prompt wording changes behaviour.
53: - **Coverage:** cannot certify arithmetic; unit/definition wording (e.g. the PM band, C2 multiple) can recur; no machine-readable coverage.
54: - **Cost:** ESTIMATE ~0.2–0.5 day; low value as a correctness claim.
55: - **Verdict:** necessary but insufficient; keep L1/L2, do not extend as the solution.
56: 
57: ### 2.2 B — Typed supplied-fact bundle + deterministic relation calculator + claim ledger (recommended)
58: 
59: - **Rationale:** separates *facts* (typed, run-bound, supplied or later projected), *claims* (detected relations) and *computed results* (deterministic). A claim is checked **against the specified operands**; unregistered relations are `UNSUPPORTED`; missing/unknown/ambiguous inputs are `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
60: - **Coverage gaps:** undetected prose stays uncounted; semantic financial definitions remain `UNSUPPORTED`; coverage is bounded to the registered relations.
61: - **Integration cost:** first slice (standalone, supplied fixture, three relations) small; automatic extraction, more classes and any staging/gating are later.
62: - **Verdict:** recommended bounded design; do **not** restart C1/C2/C3.
63: 
64: ### 2.3 C — Prose parsing / second-LLM critique
65: 
66: - **Rationale:** flexible; can “explain” arithmetic in arbitrary prose.
67: - **Coverage:** a regex cannot universally verify financial prose; a second LLM is non-deterministic, adds cost/latency, can hallucinate agreement, and is itself unverifiable. It can at most **triage or extract candidate claims**, never certify.
68: - **Cost:** ESTIMATE ~2–4 days plus per-call cost/latency; weak auditability.
69: - **Verdict:** acceptable only as a *detection aid*; its output is always an `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`-until-confirmed suggestion and never yields `VERIFIED` by itself (wrong operands/formula that happen to compute must not certify the prose).
70: 
71: **Recommendation:** **B**. Do not restart C1/C2/C3.

88: ## 4. Proposed schema/interface (NEW; UNAPPROVED)
89: 
90: First slice modules (out-of-tree standalone acceptable; paths proposed):
91: 
92: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/__init__.py` — package (NEW; D implements, B contract, C tests, E wiring).
93: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/facts.py` — `TrustedFact`/`FactBundle` + precision/unit policy (NEW).
94: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/calculator.py` — registered relations over `Decimal` (NEW).
95: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/claims.py` — claim model + (fixture-supplied) claim set (NEW).
96: - `tradingagents/runapi/numeric/audit.py` — standalone audit over saved artifacts + supplied fixture (NEW).

99: 
100: ### 4.1 `TrustedFact` / `FactBundle`
101: 
102: ```
103: FactSource = Literal[
104:   "supplied_run_fixture",        # explicitly supplied, run-bound typed inputs (first slice)
105:   "verified_market_snapshot",    # later: typed values derived from snapshot.py
106:   "fundamentals_statement",      # later: statement facts with period/availability date
107:   "trader_proposed_level",       # later: the Trader's *proposed* level (NOT verified market truth)
108:   "portfolio_user_supplied",     # user-supplied holdings/cash (unverified)
109: ]
110: 
111: TrustedFact {
112:   name: str
113:   value: Decimal | None          # None = unknown (never coerced to 0)
114:   unit: Literal["price","points","shares","currency","multiple","percent","ratio"]
115:   source: FactSource
116:   source_id: str                 # e.g. snapshot row id / statement ref / "user_input"
117:   availability_date: str         # ISO date the fact became knowable (must be <= run analysis date)
118:   period: str | None             # explicit statement period end/label (not the run date)
119:   run_analysis_date: str         # the run's analysis date
120:   declared_precision: int        # digits after decimal the claim may rely on
121:   verified: bool                 # True only for externally-verifiable sources; user/model inputs are False
122: }
123: 
124: FactBundle {
125:   run_id: str; ticker: str; analysis_date: str
126:   fingerprint_sha256: str | None # frozen portfolio fingerprint when portfolio-derived (else None)
127:   source_revision: str; prompt_hash: str
128:   facts: list[TrustedFact]
129: }
130: ```
131: 
132: Rules: unknown `value` is `None` (never `0`); `availability_date` must be `<=` the run analysis date (a post-cutoff fact is excluded); `period` and `availability_date` are distinct from the run date; `verified=False` for user-supplied holdings and for model-proposed levels. Portfolio **quantity is user-supplied/unverified**. The bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md)).
133: 
134: ### 4.2 `NumericClaim` (a detected relation) and calculator operations
135: 
136: ```
137: ClaimClass = Literal[
138:   "price_distance","price_direction","atr_distance","atr_band",
139:   "percent_with_denominator","position_notional","risk_reward"
140: ]
141: 
142: OperandRef {
143:   fact: str                      # fact name in the bundle
144:   role: Literal["anchor","level","atr","minuend","subtrahend","numerator",
145:                 "denominator","factor_min","factor_max","quantity","price"]
146: }
147: 
148: NumericClaim {
149:   claim_id: str
150:   class: ClaimClass
151:   operands: list[OperandRef]     # roles make the relation explicit
152:   asserted_unit: "price|points|currency|percent|ratio|multiple"
153:   asserted_value: Decimal | None # single stated number, or...
154:   asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None
155:   asserted_direction: "above|below|none"   # for distance/direction claims
156:   claim_precision: int           # digits after decimal the *claim* was stated at
157:   anchor_evidence: str | None    # trusted reference linking a claim to its anchor claim, if any
158:   stage: str                     # "trader" | "portfolio_manager" | "research_manager" | ...
159:   stage_text_sha256: str         # hash of the stage prose the span indexes into
160:   text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into that stage prose (evidence; never rewritten)
161:   extraction_provenance: "supplied" | "deterministic" | "llm_assisted"
162: }
163: ```
164: 
165: A relation whose class is not registered, or whose operands cannot be bound, is `UNSUPPORTED` (the class exists as a typed marker even if the *specific* relation is unregistered; no impossible enum value). A claim with ambiguous extraction, unknown `claim_precision`, or missing `anchor_evidence` for an associated band is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
166: 
167: **Operations (fixed registry):** `subtract(minuend, subtrahend)`, `abs_distance(anchor, level)`, `direction(anchor, level)`, `divide_positive(numerator, denominator)` (denominator must be `> 0`), `scaled_band(factor_min, factor_max, atr)`. Each op declares its operand roles and result unit. The calculator **verifies the relation relative to the specified operands**; it does not assert that those operands are the true or complete facts.
168: 
169: ### 4.3 `ComputedResult` (proposal; NOT Q1–Q4)
170: 
171: ```
172: CoverageStatus = Literal["VERIFIED","MISMATCH","NOT_VERIFIABLE","UNSUPPORTED"]
173: 
174: ComputedResult {
175:   claim_id: str
176:   computed_value: Decimal | None
177:   computed_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None
178:   computed_unit: ...
179:   expected_at_claim_precision: Decimal | tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None  # round-half-up of computed at claim_precision
180:   status: CoverageStatus
181:   source_facts: list[str]
182:   notes: str     # e.g. "missing atr" / "ambiguous 1.5 role" / "unregistered relation"
183: }
184: ```
185: 
186: **Do not reuse `CHECK_ERROR`** for a numerical semantic mismatch and **do not create a Q5 silently.** A later, A/C-approved change may add a proposal-only finding type (`NumericFinding { rule: "NUMERIC", ... }`); until then results live only in the standalone audit file.
187: 
188: ### 4.4 Precision / rounding / tolerance policy (exact for the first slice)
189: 
190: - **Arithmetic:** Python `Decimal` at **context precision 28**; no binary float in the calculator.
191: - **Comparison rule (first slice): NO tolerance.** Compute exactly, **round half-up to the claim's declared `claim_precision`**, and require **equality** with the asserted value/range endpoints. A different rounded value is `MISMATCH`.
192: - **Precision bounds per class (frozen; a claim outside its bound is rejected as `NOT_VERIFIABLE`):**
193:   - `price_distance`, `atr_band` → allow `claim_precision` in `{0,1,2}`.
194:   - `atr_distance` (multiple) → allow `claim_precision` in `{1,2,3,4}`.
195:   - `price_direction` → no numeric precision (boolean).
196: - **Unknown/ambiguous precision** (the prose does not state enough digits to pin `claim_precision`) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
197: - **Units:** the calculator refuses to combine operands of incompatible unit roles (e.g. a `factor_*` (multiple) with a `points` asserted unit) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` unless trusted `anchor_evidence` explicitly links them as the same range claim, in which case they are compared as that claim (§4.5).
198: - No caller-chosen wide tolerances are permitted in the first slice.
199: 
200: ### 4.5 Worked examples under this policy (document examples, exact)
201: 
202: - **Distance/direction (positive):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=255.33`, ATR `4.39`. `abs(258.47 − 255.33) = 3.14`; direction: `255.33 < 258.47` ⇒ **below**. Prose “≈3.14 points below” at `claim_precision=2` → expected `3.14` → `VERIFIED`.
203: - **Direction (negative):** same anchors, prose says “above” → computed **below** ⇒ `asserted_direction` mismatch ⇒ `MISMATCH`.
204: - **ATR multiple (positive at 2 dp):** `3.14 / 4.39 = 0.7152619576…`; round half-up to `claim_precision=2` → `0.72`. Prose “0.72×ATR” → `VERIFIED`.
205: - **ATR multiple (boundary negative):** same, but prose “0.7153×ATR” at `claim_precision=4` → expected `0.7153` (round-half-up of `0.71526195…`) → `VERIFIED`; prose “0.72×ATR” is only valid at `claim_precision=2`. A prose that states `0.72` but declares precision 4 is inconsistent → `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (ambiguous precision), **not** silently accepted. This resolves the earlier `0.7153` vs `0.72` contradiction: the two are **different declared precisions**, compared by equality only at each claim's own precision.
206: - **ATR band (positive):** `factor_min=1.5`, `factor_max=2`, `atr=4.39` → `1.5 × 4.39 = 6.585`, `2 × 4.39 = 8.78`. At `claim_precision=2`, round-half-up → expected band `(6.59, 8.78)`. Prose “6.59–8.78 points” → `VERIFIED`; prose “6.585–8.78” at precision 3 is outside the frozen bound for `atr_band` (max 2) → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
207: - **ATR band (boundary negative):** prose “6.6–8.8 points” at `claim_precision=1`: expected (round-half-up) `(6.6, 8.8)` → `VERIFIED`; the **same** numbers claimed at precision 2 → expected `(6.59, 8.78)` ≠ `(6.60, 8.80)` → `MISMATCH`. Precision is part of the claim.
208: - **PM band “1.5–8.8 points below the fill” (observed):** parsed literally, both endpoints are `points`, giving range `(1.5, 8.8)` points. If trusted `anchor_evidence` links it to the preceding `1.5–2×ATR` claim, compare against the expected band `(6.59, 8.78)` at precision 2 → `MISMATCH` (lower endpoint `1.5` ≠ `6.59`). If no trusted association exists, the first endpoint's role is ambiguous (`1.5` could be a factor) ⇒ `NOT_VERIFIABLE`. It is **not** universally a dimensional error; the auditor reports `MISMATCH`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE` for review and never rewrites the text or fails the run.
209: - **C2 ATR multiple (observed):** `anchor=258.47`, `level=250.94`, `atr=4.39` → `7.53`; `7.53 / 4.39 = 1.71526195…`; at `claim_precision=1` round-half-up → `1.7`. Prose “roughly 1×ATR” ⇒ `MISMATCH` (also outside any integer rounding), surfaced for review.
210: - **Unsupported:** effective tax rate from `net_income / operating_income` when `pretax_income`/`tax_expense` absent ⇒ `UNSUPPORTED`.
211: - **Not verifiable:** ATR missing or `≤ 0` ⇒ ATR multiple/band `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; unknown cash ⇒ any affordability/notional claim needing cash `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (no `0`).
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ## 5. Integration stages
216: 
217: **Stage 0 — standalone post-run audit (first slice; no live-path change).** A separate tool reads **saved** stage artifacts plus an **explicitly supplied, run-bound typed fact fixture**, evaluates only the first-slice relations, and writes its **own** audit file at a caller-chosen location **outside** the finalized run directory. It does **not** modify saved artifacts, the manifest or its hashes, and its retention/integrity (`audit.json` + its own checksum) is **distinct** from the authoritative report/manifest. It changes no `Finding`/`output_check`/`run_outcome`/rendering. Coverage is reported **inside the audit file only**, never in the published report/UI.
218: 
219: **Stage 1 — later: automatic typed fact projection + staging integration (needs named seams and approval).** Extracting typed facts directly from `snapshot.py`/graph, writing the audit into the staging area, or surfacing coverage in the report requires touching these existing modules, with separate review:
220: `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py`, `tradingagents/agents/state.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py::_prompt_hash` (source inventory).
221: 
222: **Stage 2 — optional render/gating (separately unapproved).** Only if A/C approve a schema/interface/quality-rule change: map a `MISMATCH` on a registered relation to `NEEDS_REVIEW` via a **new, named** finding type (never a reused `CHECK_ERROR`, never a silent Q5) and/or communicate coverage in the report without implying whole-narrative certification. Would also require edits to `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` §3.1–3.6/§6, `docs/architecture/invariants.md` INV-03/04/08/11, `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`, `docs/architecture/memory-design.md`, `permission-model.md`, and the `docs/verification/*` registry.
223: 
224: **Q1–Q4 remains unchanged until such approval.** Undetected/unregistered numerical prose remains uncounted; the audit states coverage as “N of M **detected registered** claims checked”, never a whole-narrative certification.
225: 
226: ---
227: 
228: ## 6. Acceptance plan
229: 
230: ### 6.0 Optional small first slice (price distance/direction + ATR band only)
231: 
232: Fixture: a supplied typed fact packet for one saved run (e.g. `close=258.47`, `stop=255.33`, `atr=4.39`, `as_of=2026-01-09`) and a small set of supplied claims with roles/precision. Scenarios:
233: 
234: | ID | Fixture | Expected | Seam |
235: |---|---|---|---|
236: | NVA-01 | prose “≈3.14 points below” | `VERIFIED` (distance+direction) | calculator `abs_distance`/`direction` |
237: | NVA-02 | same anchors; prose says “above” | `MISMATCH` (direction) | `direction` |
238: | NVA-03 | same anchors; prose correctly says “below” (reverse of NVA-02) | `VERIFIED` (direction) | `direction` |
239: | NVA-04 | prose “6.59–8.78 points” at precision 2 | `VERIFIED` (ATR band) | `scaled_band` |
240: | NVA-05 | prose “0.72×ATR” at precision 2 and “0.7153×ATR” at precision 4 | both `VERIFIED`; a `0.72` claim declared at precision 4 | `NOT_VERIFIABLE` | `divide_positive` + precision policy |
241: | NVA-06 | ATR missing / `0` / nonfinite | `NOT_VERIFIABLE`, no `0`, no divide-by-zero | `divide_positive`/`scaled_band` |
242: 
243: The slice stops there; it does **not** validate any frozen report. ESTIMATE for this slice: **~1–2 working days** for a standalone tool + fixture + these scenarios, **if** the team wants it before the deadline; otherwise it should be deferred. This estimate is not a promise.
244: 
245: ### 6.1 Full roadmap scenarios (beyond the first slice, needing later approval)
246: 
247: | ID | Fixture | Expected | Seam |
248: |---|---|---|---|
249: | NVA-07 | notional: supplied quantity `40` and supplied price `258.47` → `10338.80`; separately, an “affordability” claim needing **cash** (unknown) | notional `VERIFIED` (from supplied qty×price); affordability `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (cash unknown, not `0`) | `position_notional` vs affordability inputs |
250: | NVA-08 | explicit-empty vs NO_PORTFOLIO portfolios | distinct; flat not asserted where unknown | fact bundle |
251: | NVA-09 | wrong ticker/date/source/fingerprint binding | claim `NOT_VERIFIABLE`/excluded, never `VERIFIED` | fact run-binding |
252: | NVA-10 | unregistered relation (tax rate from net/operating income; weighted EPS) | `UNSUPPORTED`, never `VERIFIED` | registry |
253: | NVA-11 | precision boundaries (6.585 vs “6.6”; 0.7153 vs “0.72”; declared vs claimed precision) | exact per §4.4; wrong precision `NOT_VERIFIABLE`, wrong rounded value `MISMATCH` | calculator precision |
254: | NVA-12 | standalone run over saved artifacts | audit file written **outside** the run dir; saved report/manifest bytes and hashes unchanged | Stage 0 standalone |
255: | NVA-13 | partial coverage (some `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`) | audit summary reports counts; **no** published report/UI coverage and **no** whole-narrative verified claim | audit summary only |
256: | NVA-14 | PM band “1.5–8.8 points” with and without trusted anchor linkage | `MISMATCH` (linked) / `NOT_VERIFIABLE` (unlinked); review-needed, never auto-rewritten | claims `anchor_evidence` |
257: | NVA-L | after any Stage-1/2 change: live fixed replay | registered relations evaluated against real facts; coverage internal; independent human/C review | integration |
258: 
259: Where a class is unregistered or a relation's operands cannot be bound, the result is `UNSUPPORTED` (represented via `extraction_provenance`/notes), never an impossible `ClaimClass` value.
260: 
261: **Independent human review / C scoring is still required** for: whether a `VERIFIED` relation is the *right* claim to make, narrative quality, ownership/challenge semantics, and any promotion from audit-only to gating. No numeric threshold constitutes C acceptance or F8 recovery.
262: 
263: ---
264: 
265: ## 7. Work split, prerequisites, estimates, migration, risks
266: 
267: ### 7.1 Handoff (recorded team allocation; not universal course roles)
268: 
269: - **B (architecture):** propose `NVR-` scope, the fact/claim/status contract, units/precision policy and Stage-1/2 deltas.
270: - **A (requirements):** adopt (or not) any `NVR-` item and any Stage-2 gating; A owns requirement adoption.
271: - **C (independent tests/evaluation):** own NVA acceptance, a real cohort and semantic judgement. C owns acceptance; D does not define it.
272: - **D (implementation):** build the standalone first slice; later, the typed projection, calculator and claim extraction.
273: - **E (integration/governance):** prompt-hash/source-inventory, staging/sink/privacy, report and registry edits — only after approval.
274: 
275: No approvals are asserted or invented here.
276: 
277: ### 7.2 Prerequisites and genuinely pending choices
278: 
279: Pending: whether to do the optional first slice before the deadline or defer; adopt B (vs B+detection aid); exact precision bounds if more classes are added; where trusted facts come from (supplied fixture now; `snapshot.py`-derived projection later); whether/when any render/gating is wanted; who owns semantic acceptance.
280: 
281: ### 7.3 Estimates (ESTIMATE; no measurements, no promise)
282: 
283: - Optional first slice (standalone, supplied fixture, 3 relations, §6.0): **~1–2 working days**.
284: - Full Stage-0/1 typed projection + more classes + tests: **~4–7 working days** (beyond the immediate deadline; not proposed as a necessary immediate fix).
285: - Stage-2 render/gating + contract review + live replay: **~3–6 working days**, plus A/C review.
286: 
287: ### 7.4 Migration / rollback
288: 
289: - **Migration:** the first slice is fully standalone and additive; no live-path, enum, manifest or rendering change; it reads saved artifacts and writes its own file.
290: - **Rollback:** delete/ignore the standalone tool and its audit file; saved run artifacts and manifest hashes are untouched, so rollback is simply not running the tool.
291: 
292: ### 7.5 Risks
293: 
294: - **False assurance:** `VERIFIED` must not read as “whole report correct”. Mitigation: coverage counts of detected registered claims only; no whole-narrative badge; explicit `UNSUPPORTED`/`NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
295: - **Bounded coverage / detection:** only registered detected relations are scored; undetected prose is uncounted and stated.
296: - **Fact provenance:** facts must be from a supplied or externally-verifiable source; model-proposed levels and user-supplied holdings are unverified inputs, never “truth”.
297: - **Detection aid errors:** LLM/regex extraction is unverified; it cannot yield `VERIFIED` and must not include clearly different relations that happen to compute.
298: - **Scope creep:** Stage-1/2 touches check authority and contracts; keep separately approved and beyond the immediate deadline.
299: 
300: ---
301: 
302: ## 8. Status and next step
303: 
304: This is a **plan for review**, not implementation, not approval, and not a claim that any current report is validated. Brian authorized only drafting it. Implementation, tests, canonical-requirement adoption and any render/gating wait for A/B/C/D/E scope, design and test approval. The coordinator-observed examples (L1 historical arithmetic, the PM band wording, the C2 ATR multiple) are retained as design evidence; they are not reclassified as passed, and the optional first slice does not rescue them before review. The broader roadmap is **beyond** this immediately approved drafting work.

A claim's `stage_text_sha256`+`text_span` must correspond to the actual stage prose (a mismatch is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`), and a band/anchor link must be an explicit trusted supplied binding (`anchor_evidence`), never inferred. **`VERIFIED` on a claim means \"relation verified against the specified operands\", not \"the prose is true\" or \"extraction is exhaustive\".** The bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md)).",
  "oldString": "```\nFactSource = Literal[\n  \"supplied_run_fixture\",        # explicitly supplied, run-bound typed inputs (first slice)\n  \"verified_market_snapshot\",    # later: typed values derived from snapshot.py\n  \"fundamentals_statement\",      # later: statement facts with period/availability date\n  \"trader_proposed_level\",       # later: the Trader's *proposed* level (NOT verified market truth)\n  \"portfolio_user_supplied\",     # user-supplied holdings/cash (unverified)\n]\n\nTrustedFact {\n  name: str\n  value: Decimal | None          # None = unknown (never coerced to 0)\n  unit: Literal[\"price\",\"points\",\"shares\",\"currency\",\"multiple\",\"percent\",\"ratio\"]\n  source: FactSource\n  source_id: str                 # e.g. snapshot row id / statement ref / \"user_input\"\n  availability_date: str         # ISO date the fact became knowable (must be <= run analysis date)\n  period: str | None             # explicit statement period end/label (not the run date)\n  run_analysis_date: str         # the run's analysis date\n  declared_precision: int        # digits after decimal the claim may rely on\n  verified: bool                 # True only for externally-verifiable sources; user/model inputs are False\n}\n\nFactBundle {\n  run_id: str; ticker: str; analysis_date: str\n  fingerprint_sha256: str | None # frozen portfolio fingerprint when portfolio-derived (else None)\n  source_revision: str; prompt_hash: str\n  facts: list[TrustedFact]\n}\n```\n\nRules: unknown `value` is `None` (never `0`); `availability_date` must be `<=` the run analysis date (a post-cutoff fact is excluded); `period` and `availability_date` are distinct from the run date; `verified=False` for user-supplied holdings and for model-proposed levels. Portfolio **quantity is user-supplied/unverified**. The bundle binds to the frozen `RunContext` (provenance per [INV-04/05](../invariants.md))."

        "text": "\n```\nClaimClass = str   # a nonempty class name; membership is decided by the REGISTERED_CLASSES registry\n\nREGISTERED_CLASSES = frozenset({          # first slice\n  \"price_distance\",\"price_direction\",\"atr_band\",\n})  # roadmap adds: \"atr_distance\",\"percent_with_denominator\",\n    # \"position_notional\",\"risk_reward\"\n\nOperandRef {\n  fact: str                      # fact name in the bundle\n  role: Literal[\"anchor\",\"level\",\"atr\",\"minuend\",\"subtrahend\",\"numerator\",\n                \"denominator\",\"factor_min\",\"factor_max\",\"quantity\",\"price\"]\n}\n\nNumericClaim {\n  claim_id: str\n  claim_class: ClaimClass        # arbitrary nonempty string; not one of a fixed literal set\n  operands: list[OperandRef]     # roles make the relation explicit\n  asserted_unit: \"price|points|currency|percent|ratio|multiple\"\n  asserted_value: Decimal | None # single stated number, or...\n  asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None\n  asserted_direction: \"above|below|none\"   # for distance/direction claims\n  claim_precision: int | None    # digits after decimal the *claim* states; None = not stated\n  anchor_evidence: str | None    # trusted reference linking a claim to its anchor claim, if any\n  stage: str                     # \"trader\" | \"portfolio_manager\" | \"research_manager\" | ...\n  stage_text_sha256: str         # hash of the stage prose the span indexes into\n  text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into that stage prose (evidence; never rewritten)\n  extraction_provenance: \"supplied\" | \"deterministic\" | \"llm_assisted\"\n}\n```\n\nA named class (e.g. `tax_rate`, `weighted_eps`) that is **not** in `REGISTERED_CLASSES` yields `UNSUPPORTED`; the class is carried as an arbitrary string, so no class is unrepresentable and no \"impossible enum value\" case exists to explain. `extraction_provenance`/`notes` describe **how** a claim was obtained, not **which** class it is. A claim whose operands cannot be bound, whose extraction is ambiguous, whose `claim_precision` is `None`, or which needs a missing `anchor_evidence` for an associated band is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.\n\n**Operations (fixed registry) with named unit algebra:**\n- `subtract(minuend: price, subtrahend: price) -> points` (prices in one quote currency).\n- `abs_distance(anchor: price, level: price) -> points`.\n- `direction(anchor: price, level: price) -> above|below|equal`.\n- `divide_positive(numerator: points, denominator: atr(>0, points)) -> multiple` (dimensionless).\n- `scaled_band(factor_min: multiple, factor_max: multiple, atr: points) -> points` — this **multiplies** dimensionless factors by ATR-in-points to yield points; it is valid and must not be rejected as a unit incompatibility.\n\nThe calculator verifies the relation **relative to the specified operands**; it does not assert that those operands are the true or complete facts. 145: OperandRef {
146:   fact: str                      # fact name in the bundle
147:   role: Literal["anchor","level","atr","minuend","subtrahend","numerator",
148:                 "denominator","factor_min","factor_max","quantity","price"]
149: }
150: 
151: NumericClaim {
152:   claim_id: str
153:   claim_class: ClaimClass        # arbitrary nonempty string; not one of a fixed literal set
154:   operands: list[OperandRef]     # roles make the relation explicit
155:   asserted_unit: "price|points|currency|percent|ratio|multiple"
156:   asserted_value: Decimal | None # single stated number, or...
157:   asserted_range: tuple[Decimal, Decimal] | None
158:   asserted_direction: "above|below|none"   # for distance/direction claims
159:   claim_precision: int | None    # digits after decimal the *claim* states; None = not stated
160:   anchor_evidence: str | None    # trusted reference linking a claim to its anchor claim, if any
161:   stage: str                     # "trader" | "portfolio_manager" | "research_manager" | ...
162:   stage_text_sha256: str         # hash of the stage prose the span indexes into
163:   text_span: tuple[int,int]      # offsets into that stage prose (evidence; never rewritten)
164:   extraction_provenance: "supplied" | "deterministic" | "llm_assisted"
165: }
166: ```
167: 
168: A named class (e.g. `tax_rate`, `weighted_eps`) that is **not** in `REGISTERED_CLASSES` yields `UNSUPPORTED`; the class is carried as an arbitrary string, so no class is unrepresentable and no "impossible enum value" case exists to explain. `extraction_provenance`/`notes` describe **how** a claim was obtained, not **which** class it is. A claim whose operands cannot be bound, whose extraction is ambiguous, whose `claim_precision` is `None`, or which needs a missing `anchor_evidence` for an associated band is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
169: 
170: **Operations (fixed registry) with named unit algebra:**
171: - `subtract(minuend: price, subtrahend: price) -> points` (prices in one quote currency).
172: - `abs_distance(anchor: price, level: price) -> points`.
173: - `direction(anchor: price, level: price) -> above|below|equal`.
174: - `divide_positive(numerator: points, denominator: atr(>0, points)) -> multiple` (dimensionless).
175: - `scaled_band(factor_min: multiple, factor_max: multiple, atr: points) -> points` — this **multiplies** dimensionless factors by ATR-in-points to yield points; it is valid and must not be rejected as a unit incompatibility.
176: 
177: The calculator verifies the relation **relative to the specified operands**; it does not assert that those operands are the true or complete facts. A band whose factors are *claimed as points* (rather than dimensionless multipliers) without the registered `scaled_band` multiplication is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; an ambiguous operand/anchor unit is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
178:

180:

## Corrections applied (plan-only)

1. **`ClaimClass` is now `str` + `REGISTERED_CLASSES` registry.** Arbitrary named unregistered classes (`tax_rate`, `weighted_eps`) → `UNSUPPORTED`; removed the contradictory “impossible enum value” explanation; `extraction_provenance`/`notes` explicitly not a class discriminator.
2. **First slice truly limited to distance/direction/ATR band.** The ATR-multiple fixture moved to the roadmap (§6.1 NVA-11). New first-slice **NVA-05** is the PM band: `MISMATCH` with trusted `anchor_evidence` vs `NOT_VERIFIABLE` without. **NVA-03** now reverses the level/anchor (`level=261.61`, `anchor=258.47` ⇒ above) with prose “below” ⇒ `MISMATCH`. The malformed table (extra column) is fixed, and the first slice now includes **immutability/hash-binding (NVA-07)**, **wrong-binding (NVA-08)** and **invalid/unknown-input (NVA-09)** tests rather than deferring trust rules.
3. **Precision coherent.** ATR multiple allowed `0..4` dp in the roadmap registry, so literal “roughly 1×ATR” compares at 0 dp (`1.715…→2`, `2≠1` ⇒ `MISMATCH`); a literal `1` is not assumed `1.0`. PM `1.5–8.8 points` compares at 1 dp `(6.6,8.8)`; `6.60–8.80` compares at 2 dp `(6.59,8.78)` ⇒ `MISMATCH`; the same text cannot be re-declared at arbitrary precision. The negative boundary is now an actual wrong value at the **same** precision (`6.6–8.7` vs `6.6–8.8`). `claim_precision` is nullable (`int | None`) matching the schema.
4. **Units fixed.** `scaled_band` **multiplies** dimensionless factors by ATR-points → points and is valid (not rejected); a factor *claimed as points* without the registered multiplication is `NOT_VERIFIABLE`; named unit algebra per op; ambiguous anchor → `NOT_VERIFIABLE`.
5. **C4 trial 2 residual added** (`20261121T101520Z-3680051f`: “$4.47…below today's low of $255.33” — actual low−stop `1.33≈0.303×ATR`, `4.47=258.47−254`), stating L1 corrected only the observed fixture cases and the full narrative still has a wrong-anchor error — not “all price math fixed”.
6. **Fact bundle hardened.** Unique `fact_id`s; `stage_text_sha256`+`text_span` correspondence; explicit trusted `anchor_evidence` binding (never inferred); `period` (actuals) and `availability_date` both ≤ cutoff; first-slice facts are manually supplied/unverified source truth unless evidence-backed; `VERIFIED` = relation-verified only.

# R1–R5 repair acceptance and test plan

Prepared 2026-11-21, Asia/Hong_Kong. Baseline: `9b04330` (merge-only update; tree identical to `9c77b63`).

**Status: branch compatibility checked; regression plan unchanged; awaiting Brian's approval before implementation.** Brian clarified that the requested review concerned the synced branch, not a change in test scope. Commits 9c77b63 and 9b04330 have the identical tree 90b0da91625b6b4fc71bd68c7663026660de5acf; no code, tests or contracts changed in that update. User authorization to fix the issues is already recorded. This document supplies the concrete test plan for the course sheet's page-10 test-approval requirement; it does not claim that general authorization was approval of a previously unseen test plan. Approval of this version covers the bounded regression tests and implementation scope below. C's independent course acceptance is separate.

Source: [remediation follow-up review](../../reviews/remediation-follow-up-review-2026-11-21.md), residual R1–R5. The work plan is set aside. Existing local planning/readiness drafts, canonical requirements, original evidence and governance files are not part of the implementation write set.

## Scope and preserved decisions

- Repair the five observed failures through supervised OpenCode, retaining its authentic session and human interventions. No application/test implementation by this reviewing assistant before approval.
- Keep two public input modes, five research ratings, Trader's three actions and the Q1–Q4 authority/phrase set. Empty supplied input remains valid and is not forced to Hold.
- Keep the existing shared API, frozen snapshot/canonical fingerprint contract and staged publication architecture under ADR 001. These are repairs to the intended contracts, not adoption of every unapproved requirement-candidate addition.
- Report + manifest remain critical; terminal-event append remains best-effort. No false promise of survival through total disk failure or forced process termination.
- Formal provider/model/rubric thresholds remain unchanged. New metadata needed to bind cohort/case identity or retain pending starts must be explicitly versioned/documented as harness evidence, not added to public application result enums.
- F8 historical materials cannot be manufactured. Do not rewrite old diagnostics or mark formal semantic PASS without a valid approved population and independent score.
- Do not commit/push, alter `.env`/credentials or human-only policy files, make runtime/live model calls, or edit unrelated local drafts as part of this approval. A later live verification step can be arranged after offline checks.

## R1 — captured logging, not just direct scrubber calls

| Test | Fixture and expected result |
|---|---|
| R1-01 | Structured binding raises NotImplementedError/AttributeError with a synthetic provider-prefixed credential assignment and configured fake secret. Capture the actual logger: zero credential values; useful agent/fallback context remains. |
| R1-02 | Structured invocation raises a credential-bearing exception; fake plain model returns usable Hold text. Warning is redacted and fallback result is preserved. |
| R1-03 | Quoted/multiline, bearer [REDACTED] configured-value variants reach the same actual warning path. Zero planted values survive; benign text is not unnecessarily removed. |
| R1-04 | Inspect equivalent nearby model/data diagnostic callsites and add bounded sink tests for any same-class leaks repaired. Inventory exactly which sinks were checked; do not claim all conceivable secret encodings are certified. |

Primary implementation: `tradingagents/agents/structured.py`, reusing central `runapi/redact.py`; other logging callsites only if the same defect is found and documented. Avoid a global logging monkeypatch or circular imports.

## R2 — real result/provenance/case correspondence

| Test | Fixture and expected result |
|---|---|
| R2-01 | A complete synthetic population with application-shaped manifests/report envelopes, fixed cases, full applicable human-score cells, citations and hashes still yields PASS. Use actual rendering/contract helpers where practical; unit fixtures remain explicitly synthetic. |
| R2-02 | Declared explicit-empty case has NO_PORTFOLIO/null snapshot metadata, with valid recomputed hashes: FAIL. Also reject a held-target fixture substituted for an empty case. |
| R2-03 | Mutate fingerprint, basename, portfolio kind/as-of basis or a required provenance field independently: FAIL against the trusted frozen case definition. Do not infer expected input facts from the defective manifest. |
| R2-04 | Wrong ticker/analysis date or case-incompatible target fixture: FAIL against the declared cohort/analysis controls. Supported legitimate declared date values remain usable; do not silently hardcode an unrelated date. |
| R2-05 | COMPLETED plus non-null stop reason, invalid rating/check enum, NOT_RUN or inconsistent findings: FAIL. INCOMPLETE/pending starts are never accepted as completed quality samples; preserve them in completion accounting. |
| R2-06 | Authoritative report envelope contradicts manifest/evidence for outcome, check, rating, mode or provenance: FAIL even when report/manifest hashes have been recomputed. Missing/duplicate/conflicting authoritative metadata is invalid. |
| R2-07 | A legitimate quoted/fenced discussion of a different status in narrative is not accidentally treated as the authoritative envelope. Do not replace header parsing with a global substring test. Counterfeit unquoted metadata-like lines must not create a second conflicting authoritative result. |
| R2-08 | Preserve existing negatives: missing/duplicate/unrelated/N-A/boolean scores, invalid citation, missing artifact, wrong revision/config/prompt hash and unexposed challenge cannot PASS. Thresholds and fixed formal provider remain unchanged. |

Primary implementation: `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py`, fixed-case/runner metadata helpers only as necessary; positive fixtures in `test_score_gov004_exitcodes.py` must become genuinely valid, not be weakened to accommodate invalid evidence. Validate conditional fields and case facts, not merely file existence or a Run ID string. Document any versioned evidence/cohort additions; reject incomplete legacy formal evidence rather than silently fabricate fields.

## R3 — durable per-attempt replay accounting

| Test | Fixture and expected result |
|---|---|
| R3-01 | First selected slot is new, second already recorded. Preflight rejects before executing either; zero fake graph/model dispatches. |
| R3-02 | Before a fake runner is entered, its started run ID/case/trial is already in an atomically stored record. Start records are distinct from fabricated completed application results. |
| R3-03 | First case finishes, later case raises/serialization fails. First result remains saved; later start remains saved and noncompleted. No started run is silently lost. |
| R3-04 | Cooperative interruption or retained unresolved start remains noncompleted in the denominator; reusing that formal slot is refused. Do not turn it into a made-up completed result. |
| R3-05 | Scorer ingests the versioned unresolved-start representation, retains it in overall/cohort completion accounting and cannot count it as a completed report or passing quality cell. |
| R3-06 | Unique evidence files/records are not overwritten by two starts in one second. Reused run-ID claim is exclusive before dispatch; a collision cannot invoke the same slot twice. |
| R3-07 | Normal multi-case synthetic run saves all outcomes and still scores correctly. Diagnostics/pilot populations stay separate from formal records; existing all-start/retry/cohort policy remains enforced. |

Primary implementation: `test_gov004_live.py`, narrowly scoped replay helpers/`runner.py` and scorer ingestion needed for the versioned start records. Offline tests must not enable the real live fixture or load actual credentials.

## R4 — all decision stages receive the actual trusted context

| Test | Fixture and expected result |
|---|---|
| R4-01 | Hold debate/evidence fixed, compare absent versus explicit-empty versus supplied target long. Captured RM prompts distinguish the facts; empty and held prompts are no longer identical. All three decision stages receive the relevant trusted context. |
| R4-02 | Empty, other-ticker-only and zero-target fixtures carry no-nonzero-target instructions; the no-portfolio case remains unknown rather than asserted flat. |
| R4-03 | Positive/negative quantities and supported aliases preserve supplied facts; unknown cash is not zero, while explicit cash zero is identified as supplied. Holdings remain user-supplied/unverified, not externally authenticated. |
| R4-04 | Force non-default compaction with facts in the middle and conflicting upstream prose. Protected ownership facts survive; genuinely protected overflow fails before model dispatch under the existing contract. |
| R4-05 | Inspect report-stage propagation with scripted outputs and both structured/free-text paths. Retain RM/Trader/PM sections so an upstream inconsistency is not silently erased. No new universal semantic classifier or Q5 is claimed. |
| R4-06 | Existing final five-tier ratings/Trader actions and explicit-empty Sell/Underweight cases stay valid. No forced Hold and no new public result/input mode. Factual/rating stage distinctions remain labelled. |

Primary implementation: RM prompt/context wiring using the same `get_portfolio_context_from_state` / `protect_context` seam as Trader/PM, with scoped helper/prompt changes if necessary. Supply facts consistently and instructions to correct conflicting upstream ownership premises. Offline prompt tests cannot prove actual narrative compliance; after offline verification, current live narrative review remains necessary for semantic acceptance.

## R5 — publication outcome and terminal-event consistency

| Test | Fixture and expected result |
|---|---|
| R5-01 | Inject final rename failure through real `run_analysis_api`: INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR/NOT_RUN, no final artifacts/paths and exactly one caller-visible INCOMPLETE terminal event; no visible COMPLETED terminal. |
| R5-02 | Inject critical report or manifest write failure: same consistent result/event behaviour; cleanup preserves another run's work under existing F1 protections. |
| R5-03 | Only terminal-file append fails: successful publication retains the logical outcome with manifest durable=false, not PERSISTENCE_ERROR solely for this failure. Caller sees one matching logical terminal outcome. |
| R5-04 | Normal completed and normal engine-incomplete publication have one matching terminal row/result; final report/manifest remain immutable and conditional fields correct. |
| R5-05 | Tentative stage-private terminal metadata is not exposed as final before commit; critical failure cannot leave a precommitted COMPLETED in a caller-owned sink. Preserve valid timestamps/event shape and the single-terminal rule. |
| R5-06 | Existing EventSink emission/append and publication mocks/negative fixtures remain meaningful. Preserve best-effort enabled legacy sinks and no overwrite behaviour; do not delete a test simply because it exposes the failure. |

Primary implementation: `runapi/events.py`, `persist.py`, `execution.py`, with small documented internal staging/commit helpers if needed. No public result enum/signature change or critical-terminal-append redesign.

## Verification and supervised implementation sequence

1. Record Brian's approval of this plan/version in the authentic interaction. If a materially different contract or wider write set is needed, stop and explain the concrete choice before implementing it.

# Live-found Trader arithmetic: bounded repair/test plan L1

Status: awaiting Brian's approval before implementation. This is additional to the approved R1–R5 plan, not an amendment adopted on Member A's behalf.

## Actual finding and scope

On 2026-11-21, the C3 diagnostic (`20261121T093733Z-8c832879`) returned COMPLETED/PASSED but its delivered Trader section described a stop at 255.33 as about 1.5×ATR (6.6 points) below a close of 258.47, with ATR 4.39. The actual difference is 3.14, or approximately 0.715×ATR. PM corrected the arithmetic later, but the erroneous Trader section remained in the delivered report. This is a fresh arithmetic-quality issue, distinct from the repaired holdings-context issue. The original synthetic input was 40 AAPL units at average 190, cash omitted.

Proposed bounded repair: strengthen the Trader's numerical-grounding instruction so that stated distances/multiples are recomputed from explicit source values, contradictory upstream arithmetic is corrected rather than repeated, and unsupported ratios are omitted or marked unknown. Preserve absolute-price fields, user-supplied ownership/cash semantics, free-text fallback, ratings/actions and Q1–Q4. Do not introduce a new runtime checker, claim universal mathematical verification, silently rewrite earlier reports, or adopt new account-execution features. A deterministic financial-math validator would need a separate design/approval.

## Concrete acceptance cases

| ID | Input / path | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| L1-01 | Capture the actual Trader prompt with close 258.47, stop 255.33, ATR 4.39, a contradictory upstream 1.5× claim, and supplied 40-unit/unknown-cash context | Numeric grounding and correction instructions reach the model alongside all source values and portfolio facts, on structured and fallback paths. No invented account facts or forced action. |
| L1-02 | Three fresh real-school-model Trader runs with the above reproducible fixture | Each uses the 3.14 difference / approximately 0.715×ATR if it makes that claim, or omits the multiple; none asserts 6.6 is the difference or that 255.33 is 1.5×ATR below 258.47. Record every attempt and exact citations; no retries to hide failures. |
| L1-03 | Live free-text fallback forced through a non-supporting structured-binding adapter using the same real model | The same numerical instruction applies, output remains usable and no false arithmetic claim recurs. Record fallback explicitly. |
| L1-04 | Missing or nonpositive ATR / missing necessary price input, captured prompt plus live missing-ATR fixture | Do not fabricate an ATR multiple or divide by zero; omit unsupported distance/multiple or state it cannot be calculated. Preserve legitimate absolute prices present in evidence. |
| L1-05 | Existing explicit-empty/no-portfolio and supplied-holding regressions | Optional portfolios, unknown cash, five ratings and three Trader actions remain valid. Q1–Q4 has unchanged meaning and is not presented as an arithmetic certificate. |
| L1-06 | Current-version five fixed GOV004 cases, two predeclared attempts each, after the prompt change | Retain all starts, reports/manifests, actual profile and source/prompt hashes. Inspect ownership, cash, rating/action separation and challenge resistance in context. New evidence does not recover historical F8 or impersonate Member C's independent scoring. |

Implementation files: `tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py`, narrowly necessary related prompt/schema descriptions only if needed and explained, new regressions under `tests/member_b_remediation/`, and report/evidence notes. Application implementation must be through OpenCode. No commits/pushes, credential edits, new provider policy or changes to canonical requirements/governance.

Sequence: approval → captured-path negative/positive regressions → bounded prompt correction → immediate live Trader checks → full fixed live replay and appropriate offline suite/lint/dependency checks → contextual report update. If arithmetic still fails, retain the failure and ask about a separate deterministic-validator design; do not call it fixed.

Approval is requested because the course requirement sheet page 10 says: “no code change merges unless the tests for the change were approved before implementation began.” This new finding was not covered by the original five-repair test plan.
